item.title: Alli vows to surpass Makinde’s eight-year record in four years
item.description: APC candidate unveils ‘Oyo AHEAD’ development blueprint By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, has pledged to surpass the achievements of Governor Seyi Makinde’s eight-year administration within four years if elected in 2027. Alli made the promise on Tuesday during the unveiling of his manifesto, tagged ‘Oyo AHEAD’ (Itayo Oyo), at Theophilus Ogunlesi Hall, opposite the University College Hospital, Ibadan. He said the blueprint was designed to reposition the state through purposeful leadership, strategic planning, stronger institutions and people-oriented governance. The APC candidate said Oyo State had enormous economic and developmental potential that could be harnessed through deliberate policies and innovative approaches to improve the lives of residents. He said his ambition was to build a state where opportunities would be accessible to all, public institutions strengthened and the impact of government policies felt across communities, irrespective of their location or socio-economic circumstances. “Oyo State has enormous potential, but we must be deliberate, innovative and committed to translating that potential into tangible improvements in the lives of our people,” he said. Alli described Oyo AHEAD as more than a campaign slogan, saying it represented a comprehensive development agenda based on the expectations of residents and the need to accelerate the state’s development. “Oyo AHEAD is not just a campaign slogan; it represents a development agenda anchored on the people’s expectations and the urgent need to move our state forward. “We want an Oyo State that works for everyone, regardless of location, background or economic status,” he said. He said sustainable development required a coordinated strategy to strengthen institutions, stimulate productive sectors, expand economic opportunities and ensure inclusive participation in governance. “Sustainable development cannot be achieved through isolated interventions. We must strengthen our institutions, support productive sectors, create opportunities for our young people and ensure that every segment of society has a stake in the development process,” he added. The APC candidate said restoring Oyo State’s position among Nigeria’s leading states would require purposeful leadership, responsible governance and a development approach that placed residents’ welfare at the centre of government decisions. He said the manifesto contained policies, programmes and strategies to address the state’s development challenges across various sectors. item.content:encoded: APC candidate unveils ‘Oyo AHEAD’ development blueprint By Adeola Badru The governorship candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) in Oyo State, Sharafadeen Abiodun Alli, has pledged to surpass the achievements of Governor Seyi Makinde’s eight-year administration within four years if elected in 2027. Alli made the promise on Tuesday during the unveiling of his manifesto, tagged ‘Oyo AHEAD’ (Itayo Oyo), at Theophilus Ogunlesi Hall, opposite the University College Hospital, Ibadan. He said the blueprint was designed to reposition the state through purposeful leadership, strategic planning, stronger institutions and people-oriented governance. The APC candidate said Oyo State had enormous economic and developmental potential that could be harnessed through deliberate policies and innovative approaches to improve the lives of residents. He said his ambition was to build a state where opportunities would be accessible to all, public institutions strengthened and the impact of government policies felt across communities, irrespective of their location or socio-economic circumstances. “Oyo State has enormous potential, but we must be deliberate, innovative and committed to translating that potential into tangible improvements in the lives of our people,” he said. Alli described Oyo AHEAD as more than a campaign slogan, saying it represented a comprehensive development agenda based on the expectations of residents and the need to accelerate the state’s development. “Oyo AHEAD is not just a campaign slogan; it represents a development agenda anchored on the people’s expectations and the urgent need to move our state forward. “We want an Oyo State that works for everyone, regardless of location, background or economic status,” he said. He said sustainable development required a coordinated strategy to strengthen institutions, stimulate productive sectors, expand economic opportunities and ensure inclusive participation in governance. “Sustainable development cannot be achieved through isolated interventions. We must strengthen our institutions, support productive sectors, create opportunities for our young people and ensure that every segment of society has a stake in the development process,” he added. The APC candidate said restoring Oyo State’s position among Nigeria’s leading states would require purposeful leadership, responsible governance and a development approach that placed residents’ welfare at the centre of government decisions. He said the manifesto contained policies, programmes and strategies to address the state’s development challenges across various sectors. Alli expressed confidence that his proposed four-year administration would deliver measurable results and surpass the achievements of the incumbent government over its eight-year tenure. He also stressed the importance of involving stakeholders in policy formulation and implementation, saying the development of the state should be a collective responsibility. During the presentation, he outlined his proposed policies and strategies for tackling challenges and improving performance across key sectors of the economy and social development. He said the blueprint was designed to promote inclusive growth, restore the state’s pace-setting reputation and ensure that development reached all communities rather than being concentrated in a few locations. Alli described the 2027 governorship election as an opportunity for residents to choose a new development direction, pledging that accountability and public welfare would guide his administration if elected. Stakeholders at the event included representatives of the organised private sector, community development associations, farmers, students, artisans, traders, women’s groups and non-indigenes. APC candidates contesting the 2027 elections, party leaders and other prominent stakeholders also attended the unveiling. item.title: Duce Robinson injury update is brutal news for Florida State
item.description: Florida State will play the rest of the 2026 season not only with an interim head coach, but also without one of its best players. According to On3’s Pete Nakos , FSU wide receiver Duce Robinson will miss the rest of the 2026 season with a torn ACL. MORE : Florida State fires Mike Norvell after Saturday’s Clemson loss He got injured during FSU’s 36-24 loss against Clemson on Saturday. He finished the game with two receptions for 31 yards. Duce Robinson’s 2026 season Sep 6, 2025; Tallahassee, Florida, USA; Florida State Seminoles wide receiver Duce Robinson (0) catches a pass over East Texas A&M Lions cornerback Kaleb Miles (1) during the first half at Doak S. Campbell Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Melina Myers-Imagn Images This is a big loss for the Seminoles since Robinson is their best wideout. He leads the team in receptions, receiving yards, and touchdowns with 24 catches for 438 yards and four touchdowns. Nobody can separate like him or make the catches he makes. Seminoles quarterback Ashton Daniels will need to rely on his other wideouts, such as Jayvan Boggs, for the rest of the year. Boggs leads the team in receiving yards with 415 and has one touchdown this year. The Seminoles are 3-5 through eight games and will try to get their fourth win when they face the Boston College Eagles this Saturday. Kickoff will be at noon ET. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Oscar Goodman makes first start in Michigan's opener: 'Means a lot'
item.description: ANN ARBOR — Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. had several options and different ways he could’ve gone. With big man Moustapha Thiam missing the season opener against Oakland with an illness, Boynton could’ve inserted freshman Quinn Costello or veteran Jalen Reed at the power forward spot. He could’ve gone smaller and went with Ricky Liburd in the starting lineup. Instead, Boynton opted to give Oscar Goodman the nod and the first start of his college career. “I just thought Oscar has earned an opportunity,” Boynton said after Michigan’s 84-68 win at Crisler Center on Monday, Nov. 2. It’s one Goodman has been waiting for and working toward after joining the program midseason two years ago. The New Zealand native spent his first year on the scout team. Last season, he saw limited playing time primarily at the end of games while playing behind a loaded frontcourt that featured three lottery picks. On Monday, Goodman played meaningful minutes for the first time and had some good moments. In the first half, he grabbed a defensive rebound and threw a long outlet pass to J.P. Estrella for a fast-break layup. In the second half, he had a Euro-step finish in transition during a 9-0 run that put the game out of reach. He finished with six points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a blocked shot. He logged a career-high 22 minutes — double his previous high of 11 minutes last season. And while he shot 0-for-5 from 3-point range on a night the Wolverines were cold from deep, he didn’t stop letting it fly whenever he got a clean look. “I thought he played well enough,” Boynton said. “He was one of those guys that (had a) bunch of open shots, took good shots. What I'm glad is it didn't discourage him from rebounding and flying around on the defensive end because he still made a real positive impact on the game.” That showed in the plus-minus rating, where Goodman was a plus-23 against the Golden Grizzlies. That was the second-best mark on the team behind Estrella’s plus-25 rating. “I think I did pretty well,” said Goodman, who dealt with a tweaked back in the preseason. “I came out with some rebounds when we needed them and just kept shooting the ball. I need to keep shooting it, just stay confident in myself and they're going to drop eventually.” A little Euro step from the New Zealander‼️ 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/S6Oda6aOhF — Michigan Men's Basketball (@umichbball) November 3, 2026 According to Goodman, Boynton informed him during Sunday’s practice that Thiam was going to be out and he was going to start. item.content:encoded: ANN ARBOR — Michigan coach Mike Boynton Jr. had several options and different ways he could’ve gone. With big man Moustapha Thiam missing the season opener against Oakland with an illness, Boynton could’ve inserted freshman Quinn Costello or veteran Jalen Reed at the power forward spot. He could’ve gone smaller and went with Ricky Liburd in the starting lineup. Instead, Boynton opted to give Oscar Goodman the nod and the first start of his college career. “I just thought Oscar has earned an opportunity,” Boynton said after Michigan’s 84-68 win at Crisler Center on Monday, Nov. 2. It’s one Goodman has been waiting for and working toward after joining the program midseason two years ago. The New Zealand native spent his first year on the scout team. Last season, he saw limited playing time primarily at the end of games while playing behind a loaded frontcourt that featured three lottery picks. On Monday, Goodman played meaningful minutes for the first time and had some good moments. In the first half, he grabbed a defensive rebound and threw a long outlet pass to J.P. Estrella for a fast-break layup. In the second half, he had a Euro-step finish in transition during a 9-0 run that put the game out of reach. He finished with six points, five rebounds, two assists, two steals and a blocked shot. He logged a career-high 22 minutes — double his previous high of 11 minutes last season. And while he shot 0-for-5 from 3-point range on a night the Wolverines were cold from deep, he didn’t stop letting it fly whenever he got a clean look. “I thought he played well enough,” Boynton said. “He was one of those guys that (had a) bunch of open shots, took good shots. What I'm glad is it didn't discourage him from rebounding and flying around on the defensive end because he still made a real positive impact on the game.” That showed in the plus-minus rating, where Goodman was a plus-23 against the Golden Grizzlies. That was the second-best mark on the team behind Estrella’s plus-25 rating. “I think I did pretty well,” said Goodman, who dealt with a tweaked back in the preseason. “I came out with some rebounds when we needed them and just kept shooting the ball. I need to keep shooting it, just stay confident in myself and they're going to drop eventually.” A little Euro step from the New Zealander‼️ 📺: @BigTenNetwork pic.twitter.com/S6Oda6aOhF — Michigan Men's Basketball (@umichbball) November 3, 2026 According to Goodman, Boynton informed him during Sunday’s practice that Thiam was going to be out and he was going to start. For someone who had to wait his turn and sacrificed playing time that he could’ve received elsewhere, getting that opportunity “means a lot.” “It was awesome. I called my parents. My brother is in town, so that was cool for him to see that,” Goodman said. “I was really excited, really happy for the moment, knowing the past year was put to good use. “I've never really not played before in my career. I think that little bump in the journey helped me out a bit with resilience. I think ultimately it's made me a better player.” So did practicing against Morez Johnson Jr., Yaxel Lendeborg and Aday Mara last season. Seeing Mara’s footwork and how he uses angles, Johnson’s motor and relentlessness on the glass, and Lendeborg’s ability to be a big guard who can do a bit of everything are all things Goodman has tried to take and add to his game. The same could be said about learning from another talented big in Thiam, who practiced Saturday but didn’t Sunday. Boynton is hopeful Thiam’s regular-season debut will only be delayed by a few days, and he’ll return for Friday’s national title rematch against UConn in Boston. “I want to try as best I can not to play doctor when I’m in here,” Boynton said, “but I do believe just based off what we know, Moustapha’s just got something that’s like a 48-hour bug. He had a bit of a temperature, so we thought it’d be best to let him rest.” Regardless of Thiam’s availability, Goodman said moving forward he needs to keep trusting his shot and crash the glass harder. And as the longest-tenured scholarship player on the roster, he feels a responsibility to be a leader and bring the team together, no matter if he’s starting or coming off the bench. Depth was a strength of Michigan’s last season and Goodman will have a say whether that remains the case. Boynton believes Goodman can be a connector on offense and provides defensive versatility that allows the Wolverines to be a good switching team. Yet, Boynton added Goodman is among those who are “showing signs occasionally.” The next step is finding consistency — from possession to possession, from half to half, from game to game. “He did a good job,” Estrella said of Goodman. “He was gritty, tough. I mean, that's what we need out of him every single night.” jhawkins@detroitnews.com @jamesbhawkins This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Oscar Goodman makes first start in Michigan's opener: 'Means a lot'

item.title: Nigeria needs 10% growth to reduce poverty — Peterside
item.description: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Businessman and former Nigerian Stock Exchange chairman, Atedo Peterside, has said Nigeria’s economic growth rate of about four per cent is inadequate to generate the jobs and investment needed to lift citizens out of poverty, insisting that the country must target annual growth of 10 per cent. Peterside spoke on Tuesday at the second Oxford Global Think Tank Leadership Conference in Abuja, where he identified declining investment, corruption, political patronage and the misuse of public resources as major obstacles to stronger economic growth. He said Nigeria’s investment-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP) ratio had declined steadily since 1999, despite the optimism that followed the return to democratic rule, when local and foreign investors showed renewed interest in the economy. According to him, investors have been discouraged by an environment where access to opportunities is often determined by political connections, while small and medium-sized enterprises face harassment from regulatory authorities. Peterside called for an economy in which investors could operate without relying on political connections, stressing that public resources must be channelled into productive ventures to achieve the country’s growth ambitions. He warned against celebrating modest economic growth while corruption and the diversion of public funds persisted, arguing that procurement processes could be manipulated to enrich individuals at the expense of development. “Procurement can become legalised theft,” he said, citing inflated contracts and the award of projects to politically connected business partners as practices that undermine the effective use of public funds. Peterside maintained that Nigeria could not move from four per cent to 10 per cent growth without tackling corruption and ensuring that government resources were invested productively. Also speaking, the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, acknowledged improvements in some economic indicators but cautioned that headline growth figures did not necessarily reflect the welfare of Nigerians. Sanusi said the country’s economic growth of about 4.5 per cent represented progress compared with previous years, but argued that economic performance should be measured by its impact on people’s lives, rather than GDP figures alone. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria said the depreciation of the naira had affected GDP per capita, making it necessary to consider the relationship between economic growth, currency movements and household purchasing power. He said the economy should also be assessed through access to education, healthcare, nutrition and employment, as well as the distribution of economic opportunities across the country. item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Favour Ulebor, Abuja Businessman and former Nigerian Stock Exchange chairman, Atedo Peterside, has said Nigeria’s economic growth rate of about four per cent is inadequate to generate the jobs and investment needed to lift citizens out of poverty, insisting that the country must target annual growth of 10 per cent. Peterside spoke on Tuesday at the second Oxford Global Think Tank Leadership Conference in Abuja, where he identified declining investment, corruption, political patronage and the misuse of public resources as major obstacles to stronger economic growth. He said Nigeria’s investment-to-Gross Domestic Product (GDP) ratio had declined steadily since 1999, despite the optimism that followed the return to democratic rule, when local and foreign investors showed renewed interest in the economy. According to him, investors have been discouraged by an environment where access to opportunities is often determined by political connections, while small and medium-sized enterprises face harassment from regulatory authorities. Peterside called for an economy in which investors could operate without relying on political connections, stressing that public resources must be channelled into productive ventures to achieve the country’s growth ambitions. He warned against celebrating modest economic growth while corruption and the diversion of public funds persisted, arguing that procurement processes could be manipulated to enrich individuals at the expense of development. “Procurement can become legalised theft,” he said, citing inflated contracts and the award of projects to politically connected business partners as practices that undermine the effective use of public funds. Peterside maintained that Nigeria could not move from four per cent to 10 per cent growth without tackling corruption and ensuring that government resources were invested productively. Also speaking, the Emir of Kano, Muhammadu Sanusi II, acknowledged improvements in some economic indicators but cautioned that headline growth figures did not necessarily reflect the welfare of Nigerians. Sanusi said the country’s economic growth of about 4.5 per cent represented progress compared with previous years, but argued that economic performance should be measured by its impact on people’s lives, rather than GDP figures alone. The former Governor of the Central Bank of Nigeria said the depreciation of the naira had affected GDP per capita, making it necessary to consider the relationship between economic growth, currency movements and household purchasing power. He said the economy should also be assessed through access to education, healthcare, nutrition and employment, as well as the distribution of economic opportunities across the country. Sanusi questioned the significance of headline economic figures if poverty, unemployment and hardship remained widespread. He also warned that some economic gains could be vulnerable because of the volatility of foreign portfolio investments, which he said were attracted partly by high interest rates and could leave when market conditions changed. The Emir called for a comprehensive reform programme that went beyond fuel subsidy removal and changes to the foreign exchange regime, emphasising the need for infrastructure, structural reforms, transparency and accountability. He further criticised what he described as the government’s tendency to dismiss public complaints about economic hardship, saying concerns raised by Nigerians should be taken seriously rather than treated as opposition to government policies. Sanusi also raised concerns about regional imbalance in political and security appointments, arguing that the concentration of important positions in particular parts of the country could undermine national cohesion and the perception of fairness. He said Nigeria must promote inclusion and ensure that its institutions and opportunities reflected the country’s diversity. Former President of the African Development Bank, Dr Akinwumi Adesina, called for increased investment in young people, describing Africa’s youthful population as an opportunity for economic transformation. Adesina said young Africans needed access to quality education, healthcare, nutrition, technical skills, finance and digital technology to enable them to establish businesses and create jobs rather than depend solely on paid employment. Minister of Communications, Innovation and Digital Economy, Dr Bosun Tijani, said prosperity depended on countries’ ability to apply knowledge and technology to available resources. He cited Nigeria’s telecommunications liberalisation in 2001 as an example of how policy reforms, competition and private sector investment could transform an economy. Tijani said artificial intelligence presented another major opportunity to improve productivity but noted that countries needed adequate connectivity, computing and data infrastructure, skills, research and supportive institutions to benefit from the technology. He also highlighted the Federal Government’s plan to expand broadband connectivity through a proposed 90,000-kilometre open-access fibre network, alongside investments in technical talent development and Nigeria’s National Artificial Intelligence Strategy. Earlier, the conference convener, Arunma Oteh, called for an ecosystem approach to economic development, emphasising the importance of domestic capital markets, infrastructure, access to finance, regulatory certainty and skills development. Oteh said African countries must mobilise domestic resources and deepen participation in their capital markets, while equipping young people with the skills needed to participate in the economy. She also identified decentralisation as an important factor in development, citing electricity reforms as an example of how subnational governments could improve power supply and support economic activities. The conference also featured the launch of the inaugural Oxford Global Think Tank (OGTT) Artificial Intelligence Report, which is expected to contribute to efforts to shape Africa’s AI future, strengthen collaboration and position the continent to harness opportunities offered by the technology. The post Nigeria needs 10% growth to reduce poverty — Peterside appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: LeBron’s Wine Sip Proves The 76ers Are Finally Having Fun
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images During Monday night’s contest versus the Chicago Bulls, LeBron James sampled some red wine belonging to a fan. The Philadelphia 76ers won that matchup 126 to 107. James finished with 15 points, 7 rebounds, and 9 assists while the team moved to a 7-1 record on the season. The star player is no longer just grinding through the long season; he is enjoying the ride again. The moment happened in the third quarter when James chased a loose ball and crashed into fan Troy Clemons. Clemons was holding a cup of red wine, which is James’ favorite drink. James spilled some of the wine on himself and decided to taste it right there on the floor. He later told reporters, “I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm, how good it was. It was all right,” per ESPN . This wasn’t a planned stunt or a media event. It was a spontaneous reaction to a messy play. Sports often feel like a serious job for players, but this incident shows James treating the game like a party. He danced after an and-one layup that made guard Tyrese Maxey laugh. He also danced with Maxey later when the point guard scored his own and-one basket. These are the small moments that keep a player fresh. James explained the need for this joy clearly. He said, “Listen, it’s a long marathon. If you don’t find ways to have fun throughout it, even though you’re working, even though you’re locked in, then it could wear on you,” according to ESPN. Clemons, the fan who lost his wine, did not mind the exchange at all. He told ESPN, “I’m just glad for him to be here.” He even added, “I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” The fan threw the cup away and got a fresh drink. He now has a story that will last a lifetime. The 76ers are 7-1, and the atmosphere in the arena feels lighter. This is what a winning team looks like when the players are actually happy. A Pattern of Fun in Philadelphia James has a history of playful moments involving alcohol during games. After missing a shot in 2017, he seized a beer bottle from a vendor, feigned drinking from it, then returned the bottle. That was a different time, but the spirit remains the same. On Monday, the interaction was more direct and personal. ESPN’s Kris Rhim posted a video of the event on X, captioning it, “Here’s vid of LeBron taking a sip of a drink from a fan just now during tonight’s game.” The video went viral because it felt real and unscripted. The 76ers face the Detroit Pistons on Wednesday. The Pistons are the only team to beat Philadelphia this season. The team needs to keep this fun energy if they want to stay on top. James noted that the fans are great to them, so they try to be great to the fans by playing hard and being showmen. The wine sip was just one part of a great game for the Sixers. The numbers show they are winning, but the smile on James’ face shows they are enjoying it. The final score was 126-107, and the team took a wine sip. item.title: Eduardo Camavinga talks Vinicius, Mourinho, Bernardo Silva, Real Madrid future and personal transformation ahead of AEK Athens clash
item.description: Eduardo Camavinga talks Vinicius, Mourinho, Bernardo Silva, Real Madrid future and personal transformation ahead of AEK Athens clash Real Madrid are looking to continue their winning run when they face AEK Athens in the UEFA Champions League on Wednesday. Los Blancos come into this game with six consecutive wins, and Jose Mourinho will want his team to keep up the momentum in Greece. Ahead of the encounter, Eduardo Camavinga spoke openly about his difficult summer, his relationship with Jose Mourinho and the changes he made to his preparations. On his difficult summer and personal transformation The French midfielder began his press conference by expressing his condolences following the tragic death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel. “First, before we begin, I would like to express my condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel,” he said. Reflecting on the uncertainty surrounding his future, Camavinga admitted: “To be honest, it was a tough, difficult time for me.” Eduardo Camavinga is likely to start alongside Bernardo Silva for Real Madrid tomorrow. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “I’ve worked very hard this summer, and I’m a new man. I have more discipline than before. I’m working to repay the trust the club has placed in me,” he explained. Explaining his transformation, he added: “I went back to school, it was a very different experience.” “I worked on things I don’t usually do, discipline, for instance, arriving two or three hours early to work in the gym. My mindset has also changed. I’m a bit more mature.” Camavinga on Mourinho, Vinicius and Bernardo Silva Camavinga also praised Mourinho’s influence on his development and spoke about his relationship with the manager. “He’s a very likeable person, he’s a great coach with a rich history. Los Blancos come into this game with six consecutive wins, and Jose Mourinho will want his team to keep up the momentum in Greece. Ahead of the encounter, Eduardo Camavinga spoke openly about his difficult summer, his relationship with Jose Mourinho and the changes he made to his preparations. On his difficult summer and personal transformation The French midfielder began his press conference by expressing his condolences following the tragic death of Tenerife footballer Jesus de Miguel. “First, before we begin, I would like to express my condolences to the family of Jesus de Miguel,” he said. Reflecting on the uncertainty surrounding his future, Camavinga admitted: “To be honest, it was a tough, difficult time for me.” Eduardo Camavinga is likely to start alongside Bernardo Silva for Real Madrid tomorrow. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) “I’ve worked very hard this summer, and I’m a new man. I have more discipline than before. I’m working to repay the trust the club has placed in me,” he explained. Explaining his transformation, he added: “I went back to school, it was a very different experience.” “I worked on things I don’t usually do, discipline, for instance, arriving two or three hours early to work in the gym. My mindset has also changed. I’m a bit more mature.” Camavinga on Mourinho, Vinicius and Bernardo Silva Camavinga also praised Mourinho’s influence on his development and spoke about his relationship with the manager. “He’s a very likeable person, he’s a great coach with a rich history. But when the results aren’t good, you assume there’s something wrong in the dressing room,” he said. Camavinga’s fortunes are slowly improving at Real Madrid. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) Finally, the French midfield star spoke about Real Madrid’s ambitions. “Our job is to win every match. We’ve started the season well, and we need to keep it up,” he concluded. Camavinga’s appearance before the media ahead of the game suggests he is likely to start against AEK Athens tomorrow. Aurelien Tchouameni did not travel to Greece after being given some rest , opening up a spot in midfield. His younger counterpart could take that role tomorrow, playing alongside Bernardo Silva as Madrid look to secure another three points. Camavinga was very candid about his recent struggles and how he has changed as a footballer, and it remains to be seen how he fares against AEK Athens tomorrow. Quotes source: Mundo Deportivo

item.title: Zamfara APC primary: My mandate cannot be stolen — Kaura
item.description: By Idris Salisu, Gusau Senator Tijjani Yahaya Kaura, who contested the All Progressives Congress (APC) primary election for Zamfara North Senatorial District, has insisted that his mandate cannot be taken away from him. Kaura made the assertion while addressing a press conference at his residence in Kaura Namoda, where he claimed that he had been officially declared winner by members of the primary election committee sent by the APC national headquarters. He alleged that the committee’s chairman was taken to an undisclosed location by some individuals he described as anti-democratic elements. According to the senator, the chairman was abducted and subsequently announced a result declaring Senator Sahabi Ya’u winner, but a majority of the committee members rejected the announcement and jointly declared him winner. Kaura described the alleged abduction as an attempt to undermine democracy, insisting that the electorate would not accept such an outcome. He also dismissed the opposing camp’s claim that Sahabi had been declared winner, describing the announcement as invalid. The senator said APC members had turned out in large numbers to vote for him as the party’s candidate for Zamfara North in the 2027 general elections. He thanked the electorate for the confidence reposed in him and urged political stakeholders to respect what he described as the people’s mandate and the result announced by the committee members. The post Zamfara APC primary: My mandate cannot be stolen — Kaura appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: 76ers' Tyrese Maxey makes franchise history only Allen Iverson, Wilt Chamberlain have made
item.description: 76ers' Tyrese Maxey makes franchise history only Allen Iverson, Wilt Chamberlain have made originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . While LeBron James, Jaylen Brown and Joel Embiid get most of the attention for the Philadelphia 76ers , it is Tyrese Maxey who should really be putting fear into opposing teams. The guard out of Kentucky is one of the shiftiest players in the entire NBA. Maxey continues to get better with every game. Over the weekend, in a game where James and Embiid were both sidelined, he went nuclear. “Tyrese Maxey tonight as the 76ers improve to 6-1 this season: 38 points (15 in 4Q), 4 rebounds, 4 assists, 2 steals. This is the third time this season that he has scored 15+ points in the fourth quarter,” ClutchPoints wrote. On Monday, it was more of the same for Maxey, particularly in the fourth quarter, when he took over the game. It wasn't a particularly high-scoring night for the guard — at least until the fourth quarter. “Tyrese Maxey scored 15 of his 26 points in the fourth quarter and dished out 11 assists to highlight the Philadelphia 76ers' 126-107 victory over the visiting Chicago Bulls on Monday,” The News Tribune wrote. In the game against the Chicago Bulls, Maxey made franchise history, joining an exclusive group that includes some of the greatest players to ever wear a 76ers uniform. Maxey became just the third player in franchise history to accomplish the feat, joining Allen Iverson and Wilt Chamberlain. “Tyrese Maxey is the third player in 76ers history with 20+ games of 25 points and 10 assists, joining Allen Iverson (65) and Wilt Chamberlain (25),” ESPN’s Kris Rhim posted. This shows just how special Maxey is, especially with so many weapons around him to whom he can distribute the ball. While he has a knack for scoring, it is also clear that he can set his teammates up and get them involved. The guard out of Kentucky has been a special find for Philadelphia since he was drafted, and he continues to prove that. Now, playing alongside some of the best in the world, his game continues to evolve, with his latest accomplishment putting him in the history books alongside 76ers legends. item.title: Steelers DC Patrick Graham ranked one of the the NFL’s best new coordinators
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Barry Reeger-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Sunday, as Pittsburgh moved to 6-2 and gained sole possession of first place in the AFC North. The Steelers’ defense has come alive over the last month, thanks to their new defensive coordinator, Patrick Graham. CBS Sports ranked the NFL’s best new coordinators at midseason , and Graham earned the number two spot overall on the list. “The Pittsburgh Steelers’ defense has come back to life under new defensive coordinator Patrick Graham,” Garrett Podell writes. “They’re the league’s No. 3 scoring defense (18.0 points per game allowed), No. 6 total defense (305.6 total yards per game allowed), No. 3 run defense (83.9 rushing yards per game allowed), No. 8 third down defense (34.3% third down conversion rate allowed), No. 2 red zone defense (37.5% third down conversion rate allowed), and tied for No. 3 in takeaways (13).” “Having All-Pro edge rusher T.J. Watt turning back the clock also helps. After he had just 7.0 sacks in 14 games last season, Watt has 7.5 in eight games this season, which is tied for the league lead with Houston Texans All-Pro edge rusher Will Anderson Jr. No team has more sacks in the NFL than Graham’s unit’s 26, one more than the Brian Flores blitzkrieg Minnesota Vikings attack. ” “The Browns were flying high entering Week 8 with a 5-2 record, but they left Pittsburgh 5-3 after a 27-6 defeat in which the Steelers held them to both season-lows in points (6) and rushing yards (34). Graham is crushing it.” Graham was behind only Packers defensive coordinator Jonathan Gannon on the list. Graham joined the Steelers staff after spending the previous four seasons as the defensive coordinator of the Las Vegas Raiders. Graham’s zone-heavy defense has done wonders for the unit. Take this past weekend, for example, as the team recorded eight sacks against Cleveland. The Steelers can finally say they once again have an elite defense to help them in their playoff push as they enter the second half of their 2026 campaign. With Graham in charge and the abundance of talent on the unit, it seems like the Steelers are destined to have their first top-10 scoring defense since the 2023 season. Graham deserves all of the praise he is getting from the media. Let us know what you think in the comments . Be sure to bookmark Behind the Steel Curtain for all the latest news, breakdowns, and more! item.title: ‘So fake’… NBA fans react to LeBron James saying he enjoyed being Russell Westbrook’s teammate
item.description: Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images LeBron James has paid tribute to former teammate Russell Westbrook – but fans are not buying it. Russell Westbrook announced his retirement from the NBA in the offseason, ending a long career that peaked by winning the MVP in the 2016-17 season. He became the first player to ever average a triple-double for an entire season. Westbrook’s jersey will be retired by the Oklahoma City Thunder, and his former LA Lakers teammate LeBron James has paid tribute to him, speaking to the Mind The Game podcast . James said: “I think one of the things about Russ that doesn’t get talked about is like the guy never wanted to take a night off. Wanted to play in every single game. Being a teammate of his for that year or two, I think it was a year and a half, maybe two years in LA. He never wanted to take a game off. “Never wanted to take a practice off. Great dude. You can never, it’s not going to be one person that played with him in the locker room and he like, man, he wasn’t a good teammate like, everyone raves about him, including myself. “Kudos to him and that jacket, that Hall of Fame jacket is next.” The Lakers traded for Westbrook in 2021, striking a deal with the Wizards in exchange for Kyle Kuzma, Kentavious Caldwell-Pope, Montrezl Harrell, and a 2021 first-round pick. The move was a spectacular failure, with ball-dominant Westbrook and James failing to gel on the court. The Lakers won only 33 games in 2021-22, having lost key depth including Alex Caruso, who was allowed to walk for financial reasons. Frank Vogel was fired and replaced by Darvin Ham, who relegated Westbrook into a bench role. The Lakers eventually traded Westbrook to the Jazz in February 2023. LeBron James slammed for Westbrook comments LeBron James’ tribute to Russell Westbrook has raised eyebrows, after their dysfunctional time on the Lakers together. One fan wrote on social media: “Bron knows deep down he hated playing with him.” A second fan hit out: “LeBron is so fake. He was begging the Lakers to get rid of Russell Westbrook.” Another added: “He just playing it up for the camera, we all know Russ was a locker room vampire.” A third fan noted: “There’s always such an obvious lack of enthusiasm when he talks about Russ.” And another comment added: “Says the dude who used him as a scapegoat.” James eventually moved on from the LA Lakers earlier this year, signing with the Philadelphia 76ers. The 41-year-old appears to be enjoying his basketball a lot more right now than during the Lakers-Westbrook era – which might just have been the least enjoyable from James’ career, at least looking from the outside. item.title: 10 takeaways from Oregon State’s loss at Fresno State
item.description: FRESNO, Calif. — Oregon State lost to Fresno State 38-22 Saturday night at Valley Children’s Stadium. Here are 10 takeaways as the Beavers prepare to host Texas State. 1. Reality check Two things can be true. Oregon State can still be ahead of schedule and on its way to a legitimately surprising season amid a massive rebuild, complete with a potent offense. Much of its success thus far came by pounding less talented teams and several of the worst defenses in the country. And where OSU was vulnerable was there to be exploited by teams like Fresno State, which has talent and good coaching. The Beavers are not a College Football Playoff team. That dose of reality doesn’t diminish what’s being accomplished this season. They’re simply not one of the two most talented teams in the Pac-12 right now. 2. Oregon State was outcoached JaMarcus Shephard and his staff were outcoached for definitely the first time in conference play and arguably for the first time this season. Matt Entz laid out in detail what Fresno State picked up from studying Braden Atkinson from his time at Mercer and Oregon State’s tendencies. Bye weeks also include self-scouting. Fresno State was more prepared for what OSU showed and particularly offensively the Beavers did not have an effective counter. 3. Self-inflicted errors can’t happen in games like this Winning on the road against a team with at least comparable (if not better) talent and coaching is a difficult task to begin with. It becomes a whole lot harder with six presnap penalties and allowing five sacks with two leading to fumbles. OSU absolutely could have led by multiple scores early if not for a false start negating Jake Reichle’s would-be touchdown, if Aeryn Hampton’s foot was in bounds and if multiple other penalties didn’t occur. That doesn’t even get into defensive miscues from missed tackles or over-pursuits. 4. The offensive line may have had its worst game Houston was more physically dominating than Fresno State, but that’s to be expected. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. Oregon State’s offensive line had a brutal showing nearly across the board, with sacks allowed by multiple players in one-on-one matchups. OSU’s rushing stats are skewed by the sacks and not nearly as poor as the final box score, but the bottom line is Fresno State won the line of scrimmage and it’s not a particularly stout group. 5. Josiah Freeman was the best receiver on the field Fresno State’s 6-foot-4 receiver had a big night with two touchdowns. Freeman had a massive advantage against Isaiah Houi and performed accordingly. If there’s one piece OSU’s receiving corps is missing it is a target with the size and length of Freeman, which the Beavers are leaning on via their tight ends. But an outside target like him is hard to beat and he showed why. 6. Tackling, leverage issues persist OSU showed a vulnerability early, but against Houston and Texas Tech it was understandable in terms of talent and timing on the schedule. Tackling improved over the prior five games, but opponents’ speed also dropped. Against legitimate athletic threats, the Beavers showed their tackling fundamentals, speed, strength and angles are still areas of weakness. 7. The areas for Braden Atkinson to develop are clear Entz detailed Atkinson’s reliance on his first read and susceptibility to being impacted by pass rush when it’s not there. Of course, a defense has to have the talent and ability to do something about it. Atkinson’s ceiling is high provided he develops in his reading of progressions, grows more comfortable checking into run plays and finds effective counters to the better defenses OSU faces. 8. Caleb Ojeda came up big Ojeda’s three field goals should not get lost to the box score, particularly with a 54-yarder. At 14-9, if OSU manages to make a stop and gain momentum, the game could have changed and the importance of Ojeda’s kicks becomes paramount to the game. 9. Kickoff coverage remains a problem As the sample size for OSU’s kickoffs grows, so too does the success opponents continue to have. To allow a 44-yard kickoff return following a 14-play drive that spanned more than five minutes is inexcusable. OSU would literally have been better off kicking out of bounds, which has been enough of an issue as well. The Beavers rank 114th in average kickoff return yards allowed and 126th on a per game basis. 10. The weakness at corner is glaring Without belaboring a point that’s been stated on nearly a weekly basis, the matchup disadvantage at No. 2 corner remains the Achilles’ heel for the defense. Against bigger receivers like Freeman it’s simply a matter of when, not if, they will haul in big catches. Read the original article on oregonlive.com . item.title: How Oregon State turned a raw athlete into a starting linebacker
item.description: CORVALLIS — Two years ago, Jarrel Comer was a freshman at Tallahassee Community College and had not played competitive football since middle school. Now he’s a starting outside linebacker at Oregon State . Comer played basketball at Eastside High School in Gainesville, Florida, but began college as a regular student. He looked for opportunities to play sports again and football became the opportunity at Citrus College in California. He boarded a plane for the first time to take a cross-country flight to play football for the first time in more than four years. “I was willing to take that chance to get to where I am today,” Comer said. He had 58 tackles (8.5 for loss), including six sacks at the California junior college and got on the radar of linebackers coach Cort Dennison, then at Idaho. Dennison kept pursuing Comer at OSU, where he signed in January and arrived during the spring. Latest Beavers news Justin Joyner wins first game as Oregon State coach in blowout Atkinson, Legree join Nike’s Blue Ribbon Elite as OSU extends apparel deal Pac-12 confirms play clock error led to penalty on Oregon State in its loss to Fresno State At 6-foot-4 and 245 pounds, Comer was dominating in junior college from his athleticism alone. He didn’t know the finer points of playing football. Hand placement, setting the edge in the run game and pass coverage were not in his repertoire. Comer was there to pin his ears back and attack the quarterback, regardless of the down and distance. “They didn’t ask much of me,” Comer said. “They told me just do what I do, use my athleticism, get to the quarterback.” What Comer lacks in experience, he makes up for in ability. He consistently ranks among OSU’s fastest players in practice, which was invaluable to a team seeking more pass rush. “His athleticism is off the charts,” defensive coordinator Mike MacIntyre said. “We see him grow leaps and bounds. Playing a lot more (against Montana), he will grow leaps and bounds going into this Saturday because now he’s seen it, it slows down, he understands the different things.” RELATED: Experts release Oregon State vs. UTEP predictions, best bets, and preview for Week 4 Comer has 10 tackles thus far, including four in each of the past two games, and is already more than a situational pass rusher for the Beavers. He credits MacIntyre and edge coaches Joe Seumalo and George Frazier with helping him learn the game, particularly pass coverage. Ideally, pairing Comer with Takari Hickle will allow OSU to generate more pressure as teams won’t be able to focus all their offensive line on one side. “Teams have to respect his speed,” Hickle said. “If they don’t, then he’ll run right by them. item.title: Caitlin Clark picks what was ‘the best part’ about the WNBA Finals series
item.description: Photo by Brian Spurlock/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Indiana Fever star Caitlin Clark thinks that the Golden State Valkyries being in the WNBA Finals was the best part of the series. The Valkyries became the first expansion team in American pro sports history to win a championship in their second year. They achieved this feat by beating the Atlanta Dream in a gruelling seven-game series, which they sealed with a 68-63 win in Game 7. Gabby Williams won the Finals MVP award, as she put on a 30-point performance in Game 7. However, the likes of Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton also played vital roles in helping the Valkyries beat the Dream. While discussing the WNBA Finals, Caitlin Clark offered major praise for how the Valkyries managed to do what many thought was unthinkable. Caitlin Clark praises Golden State Valkyries team chemistry The Valkyries made the playoffs in their very first WNBA season. However, many were not convinced about them, as they felt that the team lacked the star presence that was required to win the WNBA championship. Gabby Williams made sure to bring this point up after the Game 7 win. The togetherness of the team showed that they were ready to do whatever it takes to win, and Clark had nothing but praise for them. “I feel like the best part about the Finals has been that the Valkyries are in it. They’ve been a franchise for two years. I don’t think people realise how ridiculous that is, that they’ve been able to put together a roster and run an organisation as well as they have,” said Clark on Not Gonna Lie with Kylie Kelce. “For Natalie, their coach, to get everybody to buy in, and to get everybody to believe, and they have really talented players but at the same time, on any given night, any of them can have 20 points and be the star. It seems like nobody’s bothered by that, that’s just how they are. They’re a close-knit team. That’s the coolest storyline of the Finals.” No player on the Valkyries roster averaged 15 or more points in the 2026 season. Chicago Sky and Connecticut Sun were the only two teams to have a similar stat. Both of these teams failed to make the playoffs, while the Valkyries marched on to win the championship. The key reason behind this is that all the players on the Valkyries knew their roles and fulfilled them to their best potential. Williams, who was the star of the Finals, had several off games even against the Dream, but other players stepped up and made the difference. Game 5 was a perfect example of that, as Williams struggled and scored 9 points while shooting 3-for-14 from the field. Burton stepped up to add 13 points, 8 rebounds and also had 4 blocks to help the Valkyries get to a 64-55 win. There were multiple games during the season that their bench won them. They had the best bench unit during the regular season, which averaged 34.3 points per game. item.title: Marcus Smart Proves He Still Owns The Celtics
item.description: Troy Taormina-Imagn Images There is a reason the Celtics lost their five-game winning streak on Monday night, and the answer wears a Rockets jersey. Marcus Smart did exactly what he always does: he got under the skin of his former team and turned a close game into a blowout. The final score of 109-93 tells one story, but the real tale is in the chaos Smart unleashed. He made Boston pay for every mistake with a mix of defense and dirty talk that only he can pull off. The Agitator Returns Smart knows the playbook better than anyone on the floor. He spent nine seasons in Boston, so he knows exactly how to rattle Jayson Tatum and the rest of the squad. He started by trying to get Tatum a technical foul before halftime, then drew a charge on him in the third quarter to force him to the bench. This was not just bad luck; it was a calculated plan. Rockets teammate Alperen Şengün told Ryan Hollins after the game, “He woke up everybody’s ass,” which sums up the mood perfectly, according to Yahoo Sports . Smart did not just play; he played with a purpose to hurt the Celtics’ confidence. He made the situation worse by nearly drawing a charge on Payton Pritchard, only to have it overturned on video review. But he celebrated anyway with his signature kip-up to get back on his feet. This behavior is the definition of a player who gets under your skin. As noted by NBC Boston, the Celtics got the full Marcus Smart experience, and it was a heavy dose of nostalgia for fans who remember his antics from 2014 to 2023. You might not miss his shot selection, but no analytics can measure the Smart chaos quotient. Emotions on Display Smart did not stop at defensive tricks. He hit back-to-back three-pointers in the fourth quarter to extend the lead. Then, he raised both middle fingers in celebration while running back up the court. This gesture was aimed directly at the Boston bench. Smart later explained the moment to reporters, saying, according to BasketNews.com , “Just a lot of pent-up, I guess you can call it emotions. Plus, certain guys on the bench was talking. Didn’t know who. I just heard them say something, so I let them hear it back.” He admitted that the energy was there and that he wanted to remind them what he can do. The numbers back up his impact. He missed his first seven shots but made Boston pay when it mattered most. Ime Udoka, the Rockets head coach, left the veteran in the game to start the fourth quarter, and he answered with timely shots. According to CelticsBlog, the Rockets are now 6-1 and sit at the top of the Western Conference standings. Smart fits perfectly with Udoka’s system because he can be himself without fear. As Udoka said, according to CelticsBlog , “There are some guys who have that defensive mentality, but it’s rare to have a guy who comes into the game and impacts it the way he does on that side of the ball.” The Celtics have tried to fill the void left by Smart since he departed in 2023, but nobody has taken the mantle yet. item.title: Yankees' David Bednar projected to get a 'slightly better' contract than Devin Williams
item.description: Yankees' David Bednar projected to get a 'slightly better' contract than Devin Williams originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have some very interesting decisions to make this offseason, with the Trent Grisham, Jazz Chisholm Jr., and David Bednar decisions being the headliners. But of those three, the one they're most likely to bring back is Bednar, especially after they placed the qualifying offer on him and didn't do so for Chisholm or Grisham. When it comes to Bednar, however, keeping him might prove tricky. The reason is that ESPN's Kiley McDaniel is projecting that Bednar will get a "slightly better" contract than what Devin Williams got last year, a deal in which the Yankees didn't match. David Bednar projected to get a better contract than Devin Williams did last offseason. "11. David Bednar, RHRP... Projected contract/QO: three years, $60 million (20 AAV), received QB," McDaniel writes. "... He has a slightly better case than Devin Williams, who landed a three-year, $51 million deal with deferrals last winter, so I have Bednar a notch above that." The Yankees' right-handed reliever is slated to earn quite a lot of money this offseason, with the Yankees already putting over $20 million on the table by extending him the qualifying offer. But if Bednar can reach this projected contract from McDaniel, coming in at $20 million per year over three years for a total of $60 million, then he'll likely decline the qualifying offer and sign a strong deal this November. MORE : Yankees predicted to sign 39-HR Triple Crown winner to replace disappointing Ryan McMahon Bednar is 32 years old, so a long-term deal beyond three years isn't likely, especially since he's a reliever. But with 143 saves over the past five seasons and a strong pitch combo with his fastball and splitter, Bednar is likely to land a strong deal this offseason. McDaniel is predicting it'll come in better than what Williams got last offseason. The Yankees let Williams go, as he signed with the New York Mets on that $51 million deal. If the Yankees aren't willing to pay top dollar for a reliever, Bednar might be gone too. However, with Chisholm and Grisham seemingly on their way out this offseason, re-signing Bednar might be more in play than Williams was a year ago. item.title: Gafford’s Elite Rim Protection Exposes Dallas’ Three-Point Woes
item.description: Jerome Miron-Imagn Images Daniel Gafford is the best rim protector in the entire NBA, yet the Dallas Mavericks still look shaky on defense. Opponents fall 22.1 percentage points short of their expected basket field goal rate when he defends them. That stat is huge, but per The Smoking Cuban , the team’s overall defense is just so-so at best. Gafford is doing his job, but the system around him has a fatal flaw that needs fixing now. The problem is that Dallas is betting its season on opponents missing open shots. Despite Gafford’s elite metrics, the Mavericks have shown only so-so defensive performance. Beyond the arc, opponents shoot 29.7 percent, a mark ranking 29th in the league. That number looks great right now, but it is not a sustainable plan for a championship run. If the league starts hitting those open looks, Dallas will crumble fast. The Danger of Open Threes Look at the deeper numbers and the worry gets real. Per The Smoking Cuban , opponents are shooting 26.6 percent on open 3-pointers, which is 30th in the NBA. This number sits almost eight percentage points under the league median. Put differently, teams would net roughly one extra 3-pointer per game hitting at an average clip. One extra shot per game changes the outcome of close contests, and Dallas cannot rely on bad luck forever. Worse yet, the Mavs are not forcing enough turnovers to create easy points. Mavericks opponents are coughing it up 15.0 times per game, ranking 23rd in the NBA. While Dallas ranks 14th in points off turnovers, the lack of pressure means the defense is just sitting back. They are not disrupting the flow, and they are letting teams get comfortable against a system that depends on Gafford being on the floor every single minute. What Happens When Gafford Sits? With Gafford playing, Dallas performs 21.7 points per 100 possessions better. That gap is insane, but it raises a terrifying question about their rotation. The team has no other bigs who can match his impact. Morez Johnson Jr. and P.J. Washington have not come close to matching that pro-level protection. Johnson is already picking up 3.2 fouls per game in just 15.5 minutes, which limits his time on the floor. If Gafford rests, the rim protection vanishes. This reliance creates a clear ceiling for the team. They need to force more turnovers and stop giving up wide-open looks. The defense has been splashy because of Gafford, Zaccharie Risacher, and Cooper Flagg, but the point of attack is still slipping. A defensive rating of 111.3 places Dallas 16th in the league, right in the middle of the pack.

The team has no other bigs who can match his impact. Morez Johnson Jr. and P.J. Washington have not come close to matching that pro-level protection. Johnson is already picking up 3.2 fouls per game in just 15.5 minutes, which limits his time on the floor. If Gafford rests, the rim protection vanishes. This reliance creates a clear ceiling for the team. They need to force more turnovers and stop giving up wide-open looks. The defense has been splashy because of Gafford, Zaccharie Risacher, and Cooper Flagg, but the point of attack is still slipping. A defensive rating of 111.3 places Dallas 16th in the league, right in the middle of the pack.

item.title: LeBron James Sips Fan’s Wine After Crash In 76ers Win
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James did not just crash into a Philadelphia 76ers fan on Monday night; he actually tasted the wine the fan was holding. The star player took a sip of the spilled drink after a fastbreak collision, then told reporters he wanted to see “how good it was.” This unusual moment happened during the 76ers’ 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls, a game that marked their fourth straight victory. James admitted the contact was messy but kept the mood light. After recording 15 points, nine assists, and seven rebounds, “I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine,” James said. He did not stop there. “So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was alright.” Laughter filled the room as he shared the story, showing the relaxed vibe around the team right now. A Long Season Needs Fun The 76ers have won seven of their first eight games, sitting at the top of the Eastern Conference. That kind of success often brings serious pressure, but James argues that players need to find joy to survive the grind. “It’s a long marathon, and if you don’t find ways to have fun throughout — even though you’re working, even though you’re locked in — it can wear on you,” James said. Joel Embiid and Tyrese Maxey started alongside James, while VJ Edgecombe and Jaylen Brown also took the floor for the opening tip. Every starter scored in double-figures, with Maxey leading the charge with 26 points. The team’s chemistry looks sharp, and the players seem to be enjoying the process rather than just the result. Associated Press noted that the win improved the team’s record to 7-1. Why the Sip Matters Fans in Philadelphia have seen their share of heartbreak, so seeing a player like James share a laugh with a supporter feels different. It breaks the wall between the court and the stands. ESPN reported that fans are still talking about the moment, calling it a wild sight to see during a live game. TheScore confirmed the event, noting that James drank from the fan’s cup right after the collision. Yahoo Sports added that NBA fans across the league could not believe what they saw on the broadcast. The moment was not planned, yet it fits the current narrative of a 76ers team that is winning while keeping things fresh. When a player performs at this level and still finds time to joke about a spilled drink, it signals a team that is comfortable in its own skin. The 76ers will need to keep this energy as the season moves forward.

item.title: West Ham eye Parker move after sacking Nuno
item.description: Scott Parker has been linked with the West Ham manager's job (Paul ELLIS) West Ham are expected to hire Scott Parker as their new manager after the Championship club sacked Nuno Espirito Santo on Tuesday. Parker is believed to be West Ham's top choice to replace Nuno and could be appointed in time for Wednesday's match against Cardiff after opening talks with the club. The former England midfielder spent four seasons as a player with West Ham and led Bournemouth and Burnley to promotion from the Championship as a manager. Parker, 46, also had spells in charge at Fulham and Club Brugge. West Ham are looking for their fourth permanent boss since David Moyes left in May 2024. Julen Lopetegui was sacked after just six months in charge and Graham Potter was axed after only eight months in charge. Nuno, 52, oversaw the Hammers' relegation from the Premier League last season but stayed with the east London club in a bid to lead them back into the top flight. Many viewed the Hammers as favourites to win automatic promotion, but they are currently eighth in the second-tier table, six points behind leaders Middlesbrough, after 13 games. West Ham had lost their past two league games against Southampton and West Brom. Nuno, who previously managed Wolves, Tottenham and Nottingham Forest, was appointed in September last year. "West Ham United can confirm that men's first-team head coach Nuno Espirito Santo has left his position with immediate effect," the club said in a statement. "Following a thorough review of the start to the EFL Championship season, the board of directors believe that a change is necessary at this time in order to ensure that the club's objectives and expectations remain on track." jw-smg/jc

item.title: Netflix Reportedly Working on Dana White Documentary Set For Early 2027 Release
item.description: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect Netflix did not land the UFC, but it is still getting a project centered on Dana White . According to Page Six , Netflix was close enough to securing the rights to stream UFC events in 2025 that it approved a White documentary to go along with the fights. The UFC deal never happened, but production continued, and Page Six reports the film will likely debut in the first three months of 2027. The film is directed by Gotham Chopra, a co-founder of Religion of Sports, whose credits include the Tom Brady docuseries Tom vs Time and Man in the Arena. Chopra declined to comment to Page Six. The project started as a documentary about Las Vegas before shifting its focus to White. That appears to match a November 2025 report from The Hollywood Reporter, which said Netflix was developing an unscripted project about White’s gambling in Las Vegas casinos. The documentary now centers on White, 57, who persuaded Frank and Lorenzo Fertitta to spend $2 million on the UFC in 2001. Fifteen years later, a group led by Endeavor, then known as WME-IMG, paid $4 billion for the company. The documentary was greenlit by Bela Bajaria, who left her role as Netflix’s chief content officer in October 2026, with Peter Rice named as her replacement. Netflix’s pursuit of the UFC fell apart over the size of the package. TKO president Mark Shapiro said on Puck’s The Varsity podcast in September 2025 that talks with Netflix were close, but the streamer “didn’t want to have the volume.” Netflix was interested in the UFC’s numbered events, while TKO wanted them bundled with its Fight Night cards. “And that’s what opened the door for Paramount and CBS,” Shapiro said. Credit: Jasmin Frank-USA TODAY Sports Paramount announced a seven-year, $7.7 billion deal for exclusive U.S. rights to the UFC in August 2025. The agreement started in 2026 and moved the promotion away from its long-running pay-per-view model, with every event streaming on Paramount+ and select numbered cards simulcast on CBS. Chopra will have no shortage of material from 2026. In June, the UFC held UFC Freedom 250 on the South Lawn of the White House, where Justin Gaethje beat Ilia Topuria for the undisputed lightweight title and Ciryl Gane stopped Alex Pereira to win the interim heavyweight title. White has also spent 2026 building Zuffa Boxing, the promotion he launched with Turki Alalshikh, the chairman of Saudi Arabia’s General Entertainment Authority. The company’s first event under its Paramount partnership took place in January, and it has since run cards in the United States, England and Ireland. Missing out on the UFC did not end Netflix’s business with White and TKO. The streamer has carried WWE Raw since January 2025 through its deal with TKO, the same parent company that owns the UFC, and it streamed the Canelo Alvarez vs. Terence Crawford fight that served as the first Zuffa Boxing event in September 2025. item.title: LeBron James reveals major reason behind early-season injuries
item.description: The 2026-27 NBA season has already brought several injury setbacks for some of the league’s biggest names. Teams are losing key players early in the campaign, with some facing lengthy spells on the sidelines. Philadelphia 76ers star LeBron James has shared his thoughts on the growing injury concerns. He believes the pace of today’s game is making it increasingly difficult for players to prepare for the physical demands of the regular season. His comments offer a different perspective on the challenges players face when transitioning from offseason preparation to regular-season competition. MORE: Insane LeBron James stat gives 76ers real NBA Finals hope LeBron James points to NBA’s pace as a factor behind early-season injuries Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James. Mandatory Credit: Trevor Ruszkowski-Imagn Images Speaking on the Mind the Game podcast, James discussed the injuries affecting several players at the start of the 2026-27 season, including Anthony Edwards and Tyrese Haliburton . “We go back to the pace of the game right now and I think it has a lot to do with it. There’s no way that you can simulate the way we’re playing in today’s game, to offseason training,” James said. LeBron James on injuries to some key players to start the 2026-27 NBA season, via @mindthegamepod : "We go back to the pace of the game right now and I think it has a lot to do with it. There's no way that you can simulate the way we're playing in today's game, to offseason… — ClutchPoints (@ClutchPoints) November 3, 2026 Haliburton missed the entire 2025-26 season after tearing his right Achilles in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA Finals. After working to return for the start of this season, he suffered a mild left hamstring strain in his fourth game and is expected to miss at least two weeks . Edwards faces a longer spell on the sidelines. The Minnesota Timberwolves star underwent arthroscopic surgery on his right knee and could miss up to two months . The four-time NBA champion’s point centers on the difference between offseason preparation and the demands of actual NBA competition. Players can work on their strength and conditioning, but training cannot fully replicate the pace and intensity of regular-season games. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: Islanders sign Stanley Cup-winning defenseman to professional tryout
item.description: Stephen R. Sylvanie-Imagn Images Islanders sign Stanley Cup-winning defenseman to professional tryout appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Islanders are decimated on the blue line, with Alexander Romanov likely out for the season with a torn ACL and Ryan Pulock recently joining him on the shelf with an upper-body injury. Although the Isles still have a relatively strong defensive unit, led by budding franchise cornerstone Matthew Schaefer , the team brought in some extra help earlier this week. New York signed Ben Hutton to a professional tryout (PTO) contract on Monday, general manager Mathieu Darche announced. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The tryout allows Hutton to practice with the Islanders, but he’ll need a standard NHL contract before appearing in a regular-season game. Hutton, who was part of the Vegas Golden Knights’ 2023 Stanley Cup-winning team, recorded six goals and 15 points in 55 games with the Knights in 2025-26. It was a career high in goals for the 33-year-old, who again helped Vegas reach the Stanley Cup Final in the spring, where it lost to Carolina in six games. Hutton appeared in seven games during the run, chipping in an assist. He turned a one-year deal with the Knights back in 2021 into a five-year stint with the team, which saw him appear in 10 postseason contests. The veteran rearguard had a PTO with the Ottawa Senators during the preseason but was unable to turn that into a standard contract ahead of the 2026-27 campaign. Originally selected by the Vancouver Canucks in the fifth round of the 2012 NHL Draft, Hutton spent the first four seasons of his career in British Columbia, although the team failed to advance to the Stanley Cup Playoffs during his tenure. He ended up signing a one-year contract with the Los Angeles Kings in 2019 and also played for the Anaheim Ducks and Toronto Maple Leafs. Over 11 National Hockey League seasons split between the Canucks, Kings, Ducks, Leafs and Golden Knights, the Brockville, Ontario native has accumulated 30 goals and 139 points in 575 regular-season games. Before he turned professional, Hutton enjoyed three productive seasons as a University of Maine Black Bear, recording 65 points in 108 contests from 2012 to 2015. It’ll be interesting to see if he can earn himself a contract for the rest of the campaign on an injury-riddled New York blue line. The Islanders, who are 7-5-2 and in third place in the Metropolitan Division, are back in action against the defending Stanley Cup champion Hurricanes on Thursday night.

item.title: Giants Fans Can Stream The Eagles Game On A Phone Without Cable
item.description: Thomas Shea-Imagn Images Giants fans can watch the game on Sunday without a cable subscription. Per Giants.com , the entire matchup between the New York Giants and the Philadelphia Eagles can be streamed directly on a mobile phone through NFL+. This service lets fans catch every snap from Lincoln Financial Field on Sunday, November 8, without paying for a traditional TV package. While the TV broadcast airs on FOX at 1:00 p.m. ET, the radio experience offers a different kind of access for those on the go. Bob Papa leads the play-by-play duties alongside analyst Carl Banks and sideline reporter Howard Cross on WFAN 101.9 FM and 660 AM. The station begins its coverage with “Giants Gameday” at 11:00 a.m., presented by Hackensack Meridian Health, and provides fans with more than two hours of pre‑game analysis before kickoff.11:00 am, presented by Hackensack Meridian Health, giving fans two hours of pre‑game analysis before kickoff. Radio Reach Extends Far Beyond New York For fans living outside the immediate New York market, the Giants Radio Network ensures no one misses a play. The network lists dozens of affiliates across the region, including WPYX 106.5 FM in Albany and 96.3 FM “The Buzzer” in Cortland and Ithaca. Fans in Hartford can tune into WPOP 1410 AM, while listeners in Easton, PA, have access to WEEX 1230 AM and 94.7 FM. The reach stretches even further into upstate New York and Connecticut with stations like WTLA 1200 AM in Syracuse and WLAD 800 AM in Danbury. Spanish-speaking fans can catch the action on Que Buena 1280 AM, where Nestor Rosario handles play-by-play and Francis Adames provides analysis. This wide network means a fan in Rome, NY, or Binghamton, NY, can hear the same calls as someone sitting in the MetLife Stadium parking lot. Postgame Coverage Starts Immediately Once the final whistle blows, the broadcast team does not just sign off. Giants Postgame Live, presented by Hackensack Meridian Health, begins right after the game ends. Hosted by Michelle Gingras, this show airs on MSG Networks, the DAZN App, YouTube, and the official Giants platforms. For those who prefer a deeper dive into the stats and highlights, the “Giants Extra Point” show presented by Earth Treasures Fine Jewelers offers extended coverage. The official Giants mobile app and GiantsTV video streaming app also serve as central hubs for replays and big plays. Fans can follow the team on Instagram, Twitter, and TikTok for live updates that happen in real time during the contest. SiriusXM subscribers have another option available on channel 267 for the radio broadcast and channel 823 for the streaming feed. item.title: What will 'exciting' McNamara bring to Leinster?
item.description: After much speculation, Noel McNamara has been handed the keys at Leinster to replace outgoing head coach Leo Cullen. McNamara is currently attacking coach at Bordeaux Begles, and helped to mastermind a dominating victory over Leinster in the Investec Champions Cup final in May. When he was announced, McNamara described the Leinster job as "one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby". But what will the 43-year-old bring to the Irish province when he takes over next year? Ireland full-back Hugo Keenen has a long-standing relationship with McNamara, which goes back to when he was playing for UCD in the All-Ireland League, and he said it was "great news". McNamara to succeed Cullen as Leinster head coach The pair would have more interactions at Leinster when McNamara was working at the province as academy manager and Leinster A's head coach. After five years in Dublin, where he also coached Ireland's Under-20s to Grand Slam success in 2019, McNamara made the move to South Africa in 2021 to join the Sharks as attack and backs coach. From there, he joined Bordeaux in 2023 and has helped the French side to back-to-back European titles. Keenan, who is in Ireland camp ahead of November's Nations Championship matches, said it was "an exciting appointment". "It's good to have him on board and I think that's the general feedback amongst the squad," Keenan said.
