item.content:encoded: After much speculation, Noel McNamara has been handed the keys at Leinster to replace outgoing head coach Leo Cullen. McNamara is currently attacking coach at Bordeaux Begles, and helped to mastermind a dominating victory over Leinster in the Investec Champions Cup final in May. When he was announced, McNamara described the Leinster job as "one of the most prestigious roles in world rugby". But what will the 43-year-old bring to the Irish province when he takes over next year? Ireland full-back Hugo Keenen has a long-standing relationship with McNamara, which goes back to when he was playing for UCD in the All-Ireland League, and he said it was "great news". McNamara to succeed Cullen as Leinster head coach The pair would have more interactions at Leinster when McNamara was working at the province as academy manager and Leinster A's head coach. After five years in Dublin, where he also coached Ireland's Under-20s to Grand Slam success in 2019, McNamara made the move to South Africa in 2021 to join the Sharks as attack and backs coach. From there, he joined Bordeaux in 2023 and has helped the French side to back-to-back European titles. Keenan, who is in Ireland camp ahead of November's Nations Championship matches, said it was "an exciting appointment". "It's good to have him on board and I think that's the general feedback amongst the squad," Keenan said. "I'm sure he's got a different perspective of things, by getting out of the building, going down to South Africa, challenging himself down there, and going so well and thriving at Bordeaux." 'Presence in a room' Leinster know first hand what a McNamara-led attack can do, which was evident in the Champions Cup final in May. The Irish province had no answer to Bordeaux in Bilbao as the French outfit made it consecutive European crowns with a crushing 41-19 win. After that win, McNamara told BBC Sport he had used Rory McIlroy, who had not long won back-to-back at the Masters, as motivation for his players. McNamara had also spoken about Leinster's character in bouncing back after so many defeats, and said "tough times create tough people". "Obviously, we know what he's achieved at Bordeaux and he's been on the better side of a few results than us recently," Keenan added. "You see what their backline and attacks have been producing, and I suppose that's his fingerprint on it. "I'm excited to see what he has and to work with him. I think it's positive for me and everyone at Leinster." Keenan added that the departing Cullen was "big boots to fill" after a trophy-laden 12 years with Leinster. Noel McNamara will replace Leo Cullen (left) as Leinster head coach [Getty Images] The former Ireland second row has led Leinster to six league titles and the Champions Cup in 2018, but his side subsequently lost five finals in the competition, including four in the past five years. Keenan added that the fact McNamara knows the province will help him evolve the side. "He knows the club itself and he's been through the ranks," Keenan added. "I'd like to think he's got an ability to grow the club now and grow the way we play, but while keeping how we like to play and the Leinster identity as well, so I think that's important." But for Keenan, there is one attribute that has stuck out that he believes will help McNamara shift from an attacking coach to head coach. "His man-management and his presence in a room," the 30-year-old continued. "I still remember it from the get-go, from when he was a head coach back in the day with how well he speaks. "I'm sure that's the same again, and I've talked about the technical points on the backs and the attack that I think he can bring as well, so it's exciting."

item.title: After rocky exhibitions, Northwestern found some answers
item.description: Two exhibition losses left Northwestern with more questions than answers. After a 94-59 loss to Iowa State, the Wildcats spent the last week trying to fix what went wrong. On Monday night, they showed they made some progress. NU opened the regular season with an 86-60 win over Binghamton in a game it never trailed. The ‘Cats shot 55.8% from the field, including 72% in the first half, and stayed true to the Northwestern way, committing just eight turnovers. This comes just two weeks after the Wildcats committed 20 turnovers against Illinois State and shot 32.8% against Iowa State. “We just talked about it; none of those stats matter at the end of the day,” Collins said after the game. “I thought our guys came out and had great energy. Thought we played with great confidence.” Collins said postgame that he and his staff had spent the week working out the kinks in the defense and added more offensive sets to help put the ball in the right hands. The results showed that, as the Wildcats got out in transition after stops, kept the ball moving and made it difficult for Binghamton to find good shots. The ‘Cats dished out 23 assists in the win and had 18 points off of 12 Bearcat turnovers, and outscored them in transition, 14-2. “23 assists, eight turnovers,” Collins said. “That’s Northwestern basketball.” As in the exhibition games, the offense once again ran through sophomore Jake West, who finished just one assist shy of his career-high at 12, while adding 20 points on 6-for-9 shooting and going 6-for-6 from the line. Most of that production came in the first half, when he had 14 points and eight assists, working off of ball screens. Collins praised West for how Northwestern had finished last season and carried that into the offseason. Collins said West has grown from the quiet voice he was in his freshman year into one of the team’s most vocal leaders, alongside junior Angelo Ciaravino, who make up two-thirds of the returners, along with sophomore Phoenix Gill. Collins compared West’s value to the impact quarterback Aidan Chiles has on Northwestern football next door at Ryan Field. “You guys are seeing it. Our football team, right? When you have a great quarterback, you have a chance, and that’s no different than in basketball,” Collins said. “When that position is in a good spot, you have poise, you have leadership, and you have a guy making good decisions.” Collins said it was Northwestern’s first 20-point, 10-assist game since Bryant McIntosh, the legendary former Wildcats point guard and current assistant coach. item.content:encoded: Two exhibition losses left Northwestern with more questions than answers. After a 94-59 loss to Iowa State, the Wildcats spent the last week trying to fix what went wrong. On Monday night, they showed they made some progress. NU opened the regular season with an 86-60 win over Binghamton in a game it never trailed. The ‘Cats shot 55.8% from the field, including 72% in the first half, and stayed true to the Northwestern way, committing just eight turnovers. This comes just two weeks after the Wildcats committed 20 turnovers against Illinois State and shot 32.8% against Iowa State. “We just talked about it; none of those stats matter at the end of the day,” Collins said after the game. “I thought our guys came out and had great energy. Thought we played with great confidence.” Collins said postgame that he and his staff had spent the week working out the kinks in the defense and added more offensive sets to help put the ball in the right hands. The results showed that, as the Wildcats got out in transition after stops, kept the ball moving and made it difficult for Binghamton to find good shots. The ‘Cats dished out 23 assists in the win and had 18 points off of 12 Bearcat turnovers, and outscored them in transition, 14-2. “23 assists, eight turnovers,” Collins said. “That’s Northwestern basketball.” As in the exhibition games, the offense once again ran through sophomore Jake West, who finished just one assist shy of his career-high at 12, while adding 20 points on 6-for-9 shooting and going 6-for-6 from the line. Most of that production came in the first half, when he had 14 points and eight assists, working off of ball screens. Collins praised West for how Northwestern had finished last season and carried that into the offseason. Collins said West has grown from the quiet voice he was in his freshman year into one of the team’s most vocal leaders, alongside junior Angelo Ciaravino, who make up two-thirds of the returners, along with sophomore Phoenix Gill. Collins compared West’s value to the impact quarterback Aidan Chiles has on Northwestern football next door at Ryan Field. “You guys are seeing it. Our football team, right? When you have a great quarterback, you have a chance, and that’s no different than in basketball,” Collins said. “When that position is in a good spot, you have poise, you have leadership, and you have a guy making good decisions.” Collins said it was Northwestern’s first 20-point, 10-assist game since Bryant McIntosh, the legendary former Wildcats point guard and current assistant coach. West let him hear it in the locker room, joking that McIntosh subbed him out because “he knew how many assists I had.” Of those 12 assists, five went to graduate transfer Jack Karasinski, including four of his seven made threes that night. He finished with a team-high 24 points on 8-for-12 shooting and 7-for-11 from deep, and was the first Wildcat to hit seven threes since Ty Berry did so two years ago. “I like to say I have delusional confidence out there,” Karasinski said. “Once I touch it, it’s going up.” That was prevalent in the game. After airballing a three in the second half, Karasinski showed short-term memory, coming right back down the floor and firing a three from well behind the arc, which fell true on his second attempt. Graduate transfer LA Pratt showed that too. Pratt had struggled in the two exhibition games, including going 1-for-7 from the field and having five turnovers against Illinois State. After the misses, Pratt’s shot started to fall. “I kind of saw, let the air out of the balloon and kind of got him going,” Collins said. Pratt finished the game with 19 points on 6-for-12 shooting, including a big three with time dwindling at the end of the first half, when he pulled up from deep to put Northwestern up 51-35 at the break. The program also made a shocking announcement just over an hour before tip-off that the Wildcats would be without fourth-year big man Luke McEldon, who is taking a leave of absence from the program for an “indefinite” time. Collins confirmed postgame and declined to share more details out of respect for his privacy. Without McEldon, who started the two exhibition games, junior Okku Federiko took over at center — a position he doesn’t typically play — and kept the team afloat in his 23 minutes, finishing plus-20 in that time. The problems were still there. The second half was less tidy, with the team shooting 41% and going 5-for-18 from deep. Bench production also left much to be desired, with the reserves combining for just six points. Collins said he’s trying to figure it all out on the fly. “We’re such a work in progress,” Collins said. “I’m learning these guys. We’ve already made a number of adjustments even since we started playing exhibition games.” The win gives them a nice confidence boost, but one good night doesn’t settle every question raised in October. But just a week after Collins told his team their season would be defined by how they responded, the Wildcats responded well. They’ll look to build on that in the non-conference schedule, when they play host to Stony Brook this Friday, Nov. 6, at 7 p.m. CST.

item.title: Jon Rahm’s Brutal Truth About LIV Golf’s Failed Pivot
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images Jon Rahm walked away from LIV Golf’s next phase because the new direction felt wrong to him. He told reporters at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship that he “wasn’t thrilled” with the changes proposed for LIV 2.0. The 31-year-old Spaniard decided the future plan lacked the special team elements that defined the original project. His departure signals a clear break from a league trying to restructure after losing its main financial backer. Why The New Plan Failed To Impress Rahm liked the initial concept of the league but drew a hard line at the new proposals. He stated at a press conference, “As much as I liked the project and the idea on, let’s say, LIV 1.0, I wasn’t thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0 and I just wasn’t willing to follow that path.” The league is now attempting a relaunch after Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund pulled its support. This move required the company to file for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and cancel existing player contracts. Rahm gave up claims against the bankruptcy estate, reported to be worth up to $150 million, but kept his team’s intellectual property. He simply did not see the value in the new model. The former world number one felt the new proposals drifted too far from team golf. He noted, “It wasn’t anything special, anything that stood out. I just didn’t like what they were going with 2.0.” There were too many unknowns for him to commit. The structure seemed to shift toward a regular tournament format rather than the team competition that attracted players initially. Rahm called the new approach “more of a regular tournament” and said it “wasn’t really ever much of a consideration.” The Road Back To The DP World Tour With the LIV door closed, Rahm is focusing on his return to the DP World Tour. He is set to play at the Abu Dhabi Aldar Championship this week. He admitted he is currently “rusty” after a long flight and a break from practice. Their daughter Begona was expected by his wife Kelley, necessitating the break. His current standing on the Race to Dubai rankings sits at 51st. He faces a potential one-year suspension if he wishes to return to the PGA Tour. He acknowledged that Brooks Koepka managed to return through specific circumstances, but Rahm remains unsure if those same doors will open for him. He said, “Obviously, Brooks was able to go back through certain circumstances.” If a suspension is required, he views it as a chance to play on the DP World Tour for a year. He added, “But if I have to fulfil a one-year suspension, I think it’s a pretty good position to be that a worst-case scenario I get to play on a wonderful tour (DP World Tour) for a whole year.” A Final Look At The Deal Rahm is realistic about the financial terms he might face compared to other players. He doubts he will get the same deal as Brooks Koepka, which included a five million US dollar charitable donation. He stated, “I seriously doubt I get offered the same deal that Brooks did, but if

item.title: LeBron James Sips Wine While Sixers Crush Bulls
item.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images LeBron James is averaging his lowest scoring numbers ever at 16.4 points, yet he helped lead Philadelphia to a dominant 126-107 win over the Chicago Bulls on Monday night. The 41-year-old star is shooting just 45 percent from the field, a stat that looks rough on paper but didn’t stop the Sixers from securing their fourth straight victory. While the stats show a dip in his usual scoring output, the game showed a different side of the legend in action. A Viral Sip and a Massive Dunk The most talked-about moment didn’t come from a bucket but from behind the basket where James grabbed a cup from a fan named Troy Clemens. According to Heavy.com , the season-ticket holder offered the star some wine and James reportedly took a sip during the second minute of the contest. This viral clip spread across social media quickly, showing a rare, relaxed moment for the veteran leader. An emphatic double-pump jam by James, occurring just before that interaction, netted the 76ers’ first field goal of the game. That powerful dunk came less than two minutes into the action, proving he still has explosive power despite his age. James is set to turn 42 years old in just under two months, making his current performance even more impressive for many observers. Tyrese Maxey, Joel Embiid, and Jaylen Brown now shoulder most scoring duties as his significantly altered role requires deferring to them. This change has allowed him to focus more on defense, where his lesser involvement on offense has freed him up to be a force on the other end of the floor. He is averaging 7.0 rebounds and 7.0 assists per contest, showing he still controls the game without needing to be the primary scorer. Edgecombe’s Perfect Half and a Broken Defense Edgecombe finished the first half a perfect 7-of-7 from the field, including one catch-and-shoot three-pointer that added to his impressive night. He turned into the Sixers’ version of a deep threat, running go routes that the Bulls either could not or would not stop for 15 first-half points. This defensive breakdown allowed Philadelphia to coast to a 126-107 win, as reported by PHLY Sports . Because James and Maxey distributed the ball well as passers, three 76ers players scored 20 or more points in the game. Maxey led the team with 26 points and racked up seven assists in the first half alone to match LeBron. The team’s biggest star has taken on a less scoring‑heavy role. The Bulls will need to tighten up their transition defense if they hope to stop this balanced Philadelphia offense in future matchups.

item.title: Francesco Bagnaia counting down days until end of Ducati MotoGP tenure
item.description: Motorsport photo Francesco Bagnaia says the last three rounds of the 2026 MotoGP struggles will be about “surviving”, with no solution in sight for his ongoing issues with Ducati’s GP26. The three-time world champion had high hopes from last weekend’s Malaysian Grand Prix, having identified Sepang as his best opportunity to score a big result before leaving the Borgo Panigale marque at the end of the year. Bagnaia had managed to ride through his bike problems at last year’s Malaysian GP to secure pole position and a Sprint victory, giving him confidence that he could perform well again this time around. But after qualifying 10th on the grid and smashing his windscreen in frustration, the Italian could only muster a 13th place result on Sunday, having even slipped outside the points at one stage. Asked whether he was counting the days until the end of the year, Bagnaia replied: “[Yes, but] not just from this moment.” Pressed further as to what he could expect from the final races, with the evidence that the Ducati had failed to work to his liking at one of his favourite tracks, he replied “surviving”. Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team Francesco Bagnaia, Ducati Team Bagnaia has been suffering from grip issues since the start of the year, but was still able to secure some headline results in the first half of the season - including four consecutive Sunday podiums and a sprint win at Brno. However, his form nosedived after the summer break, with the last eight rounds yielding a pair of sixth-place sprint finishes as his best results. The 29-year-old said he had been unable to push for even a single lap at Sepang on Sunday, with his performance deteriorating particularly badly in the closing stages of the race. “It looked exactly like I was expecting, no more no less,” he admitted. “On Saturday, I was just lucky that it started to rain. But on Sunday, I saw that my limit was the grip. I tried to manage it. “Even managing it, after five laps I was without the rear tyre and I needed to start thinking about just finishing the race. The last lap I did was 2m05.1s. For me it's something unbelievable, considering what I know that I can do here, that is what it is. “It's like this and we need to accept it. Three to go and try to do the maximum.” Asked how difficult it was to reach the finish on worn tyres, he replied: “It was dead easy, because I wasn't able to do any push lap. It was like doing an easy run.” Bagnaia’s last lap at Sepang - a 2m05.143s - was a full two seconds slower than his team-mate Marc Marquez , who had backed off considerably as he celebrated his seventh grand prix win of the season. Among other Ducati riders, Alex Marquez and Franco Morbidelli were also able to lap within the 2m02s bracket in the closing stages of the race, while Fabio di Giannantonio ’s pace dipped into the mid 2m03s. item.title: New York Post makes Game of Thrones quip as John Harbaugh teases Giants trade deadline bombshell
item.description: New York Post makes Game of Thrones quip as John Harbaugh teases Giants trade deadline bombshell appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . As the NFL trade deadline approaches, John Harbaugh and the New York Giants may be buyers, which resulted in The New York Post making a pun involving Game of Thrones . Today’s issue of The New York Post devoted two pages to the Giants, including rumors involving the trade deadline. Harbaugh said he’d take “any call” about trades before the deadline next week. Giants spread in today’s New York Post. https://t.co/aICaofYRia Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) — Paul Schwartz (@NYPost_Schwartz) November 3, 2026 The piece about the trade deadline is dubbed “Game of Phones.” We’ll see how active Harbaugh’s phone is over the next week or so. Will the Giants make moves at the trade deadline? Vincent Carchietta-Imagn Images The Giants have a week to make any trades before the deadline at 4 pm EST on Nov. 10. There have been rampant rumors about them making moves. While they are 4-2-1 and in first place in the NFC East, the Giants should not be content. They could use some help at the running back position. Cam Skattebo, the team’s starter, was benched in a previous game. Tyrone Tracy Jr. was also placed on injured reserve last week with a hamstring injury. Najee Harris was brought in during the offseason but was cut after making comments about the team’s running back rotation. The team still has Devin Singletary and Greg Desrosiers Jr. on the roster. The Giants are coming off their bye in Week 8. They won an overtime thriller against the Houston Texans before their break. Their next game is against the Philadelphia Eagles, who are reeling after losing Jalen Hurts for the season, in Week 9. Philly has lost seven games in a row after starting the year 2-0. Harbaugh’s tenure with the Giants is off to a hot start. Given the state of the NFC East, they have a good chance to win the division. This comes after Harbaugh’s 18-year career with the Baltimore Ravens, during which he won a Super Bowl. Related: Giants’ John Harbaugh admits calling AFC team as trade deadline looms Related: The reason Giants RB Cam Skattebo was fined $7,073 after Texans game

item.title: Warriors Star Draymond Green Ejected After Fiery Scuffle with Suns’ Dillon Brooks
item.description: Draymond Green and Dillon Brooks on Nov. 2, 2026 Credit: NBA on ESPN/X.com NEED TO KNOW Warriors’ Draymond Green was ejected after he put his hands on Dillon Brooks’ neck on Monday, Nov. 2 Brooks ran up to Green after the Warriors star committed a hard foul on Khaman Maluach, throwing him to the floor Steph Curry said Green’s scuffle with Brooks “lit a fire in” the Warriors, who went on to win 116-113 Draymond Green was ejected from the Golden State Warriors’ matchup against the Phoenix Suns on Monday, Nov. 2 after he and Dillons Brooks got into it in the third quarter. The Warriors were down by seven points when Green, 36, committed a hard foul on Suns center Khaman Maluach, throwing him to the floor on a shot attempt. Maluach, 20, remained on the floor for a moment as an upset Brooks, 30, ran up to Green. Green grabbed Brooks by the neck of his jersey and the two began shoving each other in the face, shoulders and neck as their teammates tried to break up the scuffle. The Warriors’ broadcasters said it was Yusef Wright, a member of Golden State’s security and longtime bodyguard for Steph Curry , who was able to pull Green away from his opponent. “You don’t want that to escalate at all,” the announcer said after. Draymond Green was assessed a double technical on this play and was ejected. pic.twitter.com/uCmsTQxmcX — NBA on ESPN (@ESPNNBA) November 3, 2026 Brooks received a technical foul for his part in the scuffle, while Green was handed two technical fouls, resulting in an immediate ejection. Monday’s ejection was Green’s 31st since his NBA career began 15 years ago, per ESPN . Speaking to reporters after the game, a 116-113 victory for Golden State, Brooks claimed he was “just trying to de-escalate” the situation between Green and Maluach after the hard foul, according to ESPN . “He was just tweaking all game,” Brooks claimed of Green, who did not speak with the media on Monday. Draymond Green on Nov. 2, 2026 in San Francisco, CA Credit: Noah Graham/NBAE via Getty Meanwhile, Warriors head coach Steve Kerr chalked up the fiery moment to healthy competition between athletes. “That’s just the greatest NBA basketball players on earth competing,” Kerr said , noting, “Nothing serious happened.” Follow your favorite athletes on and off the field with PEOPLE’s free sports newsletter — sign up now! Curry said Green “lit a fire in all of us” and told reporters he was “glad” he and his teammates were able to pull off the win. “We had to respond,” said Curry. Next, the Warriors will host the Miami Heat on Thursday, Nov. 5. Read the original article on People

item.title: Spanish police open possible involuntary manslaughter investigation after tragic death of Tenerife’s Jesús de Miguel
item.description: Spanish police open possible involuntary manslaughter investigation after tragic death of Tenerife’s Jesús de Miguel An official police investigation has been opened, following the tragic events in Monday’s meeting between Tenerife and FC Andorra in Spanish football’s 2nd tier. Yesterday’s Segunda clash was abandoned late on, after Tenerife star Jesús de Miguel was stretchered from the field of play amid alarming scenes. Taken out by a flying challenge from Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono, De Miguel was taken straight to a nearby hospital, where he was placed in intensive care after suffering a cardiac arrest. In tragic news for the 30-year-old’s family, friends and all at Tenerife, De Miguel’s death was confirmed on Tuesday. Owing to the nature of the incident which culminated in his passing, an official investigation has since been opened by not only the Spanish football authorities, but also the National Police. As per a report from ESPN : ‘Spanish police have opened an investigation into possible involuntary manslaughter after Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel died following an on-field collision.’ It is added that ‘under Spanish law, deaths from non-natural causes, including accidents, are subject to judicial investigation.’ We at Get Football send our condolences to all affected by Jesús de Miguel’s untimely passing. Conor Laird – GSFN

item.title: The Hornets Look Lost Without LaMelo Ball
item.description: Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) smiles as he answers questions following the win over the Milwaukee Bucks at Target Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Charlotte Hornets just got their doors blown off again, falling 124-91 to the Detroit Pistons and dropping to 3-5. The painful truth is staring them in the face: this offense doesn’t know how to function without LaMelo Ball . The former franchise point guard, now a Minnesota Timberwolf after Charlotte traded Ball for Naz Reid and draft capital, was the engine that made everything go. Without him, the Hornets don’t have an identity. It’s becoming evident that trading Ball wasn’t a move made in the interest of winning basketball games — at least not right now. Charlotte’s Offense May Be the Worst in the League Nov 2, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Kevin Huerter (27) defends against Charlotte Hornets guard Dennis Schroder (17) during the second half at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Coming into the new season, the offense was expected to still be good — even without Ball. After all, Brandon Miller , Coby White , and Kon Knueppel are still on the team. However, that has not been the case. In eight games, the Hornets have failed to reach the 25-point mark in a quarter 18 times, meaning they’re coming up short in 56.25 percent of all quarters played. This has led to the Hornets owning the worst offensive rating in the league (100.5). A major contributing factor is that the high volume of three-pointers launched isn’t converting to points. The only player shooting above a 35 percent clip from beyond the arc is Grayson Allen . His consistent three-point shooting (currently 46.6% at 7.3 attempts per game) is what makes Allen a Sixth Man of the Year candidate . As a whole, the Hornets are shooting 29.6 percent from three-point range, ranking second-to-last in the league. If Charlotte were shooting closer to their uber-efficient 37.8 percent from last season, the narrative would be completely different. Historic Offense When LaMelo Ball Led the Way The Hornets became one of the teams to watch last season during their midseason turnaround. Led by Ball, they looked virtually unstoppable in a lot of games. As a matter of fact, the Hornets had the largest average margin of victory (in wins) at +18.1 points last season. Not only was this the biggest margin in the league, but it was the largest in league history. Ball’s gravity as a lethal shooter and playmaker gave his teammates plenty of great looks. With that creativity gone, those created advantages have been erased. Ball had things that he needed to improve on, but the talent was undeniable. Hornets offense last 15 games: 1st (121.6) Hornets defense last 15 games: 5th (110.4) Hornets net rating last 15 games: 1st (+11.2) https://t.co/Zj4aVT2pyr pic.twitter.com/MpCsBGOp5P — Basketball University (@UofBasketball) January 27, 2026 Kn
item.content:encoded: Nov 2, 2026; Minneapolis, Minnesota, USA; Minnesota Timberwolves guard LaMelo Ball (1) smiles as he answers questions following the win over the Milwaukee Bucks at Target Center. | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Jimmy Vik The Charlotte Hornets just got their doors blown off again, falling 124-91 to the Detroit Pistons and dropping to 3-5. Charlotte’s Offense May Be the Worst in the League Nov 2, 2026; Charlotte, North Carolina, USA; Detroit Pistons guard Kevin Huerter (27) defends against Charlotte Hornets guard Dennis Schroder (17) during the second half at Spectrum Center. Mandatory Credit: Jim Dedmon-Imagn Images Coming into the new season, the offense was expected to still be good — even without Ball. If Charlotte were shooting closer to their uber-efficient 37.8 percent from last season, the narrative would be completely different. Hornets offense last 15 games: 1st (121.6) Hornets defense last 15 games: 5th (110.4) Hornets net rating last 15 games: 1st (+11.2) https://t.co/Zj4aVT2pyr pic.twitter.com/MpCsBGOp5P — Basketball University (@UofBasketball) January 27, 2026 Knueppel’s return from injury is still in the ramping-up phase, and White was on a minute restriction for his first game back, but it’s hard to still believe that they can recreate the magic from last season. General Manager Jeff Peterson betting against Ball hinged on reasons like whether he was actually injury-prone or couldn’t embrace physicality. The Last Word Peterson asked Hornets fans for patience . So far, though, his plan to trade Ball is going sideways, and that patience runs thin when you’ve already been decimated on your home court twice this season. The Hornets’ offense is in shambles, and there’s an argument to be made that Knueppel could elevate it from being the worst offense in the league. But it’s hard to imagine this offense being anywhere close to how great it was last season with Ball. One of the biggest gambles that this organization has taken looks to have already backfired. Watching Ball have success in Minnesota while Charlotte struggles to do anything on offense is exactly what fans feared would happen when you remove one of the most impactful offensive creators in the NBA. Maybe Hornets basketball will look different when everyone is healthy, but the more likely scenario from the eight-game sample is that this offense won’t reach the heights of last season. item.title: Seahawks hit with harsh reality check after getting ‘smacked physically’ by Bears
item.description: Matt Kartozian-Imagn Images Seahawks hit with harsh reality check after getting ‘smacked physically’ by Bears appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Seattle Seahawks were humbled on Monday night, after losing 34-17 to the Chicago Bears. The usually reliable Seahawks defense got exposed, especially in the red zone. Seattle is now getting issued a stern warning by an NFL insider. “The worst red zone defense in the NFL…..no answers tonight. The Bears out hit them, the Bears out played them,” analyst Brock Huard said, per Seattle Sports. The #Seahawks got "smacked physically in a way we have not in years," says @BrockHuard in his reaction to the 34-17 loss, presented by @Puyallup_Tribe . Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) More reaction & analysis at https://t.co/sy672x5HGZ . pic.twitter.com/AhXHoDB6oX — Seattle Sports (@SeattleSports) November 3, 2026 It was certainly a tough night for Seattle. Offensively, the team couldn’t run the football. Defensively, Seattle got absolutely torched in the red zone. Huard went on to describe the game, and held absolutely nothing back. “We got smacked physically in a way we have not in years,” Huard added. His words ring true. Seattle’s defense allowed 363 total yards to the Bears. Seattle also went just 1-for-11 on third down, in a rough performance . “We got beat. No other way to sugar coat it,” Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald said, per the Associated Press. “When you look at the things that it takes to win in our league, we didn’t do those things and they did.” Seattle seemed especially bothered by Bears defensive tackle Jeffery Simmons . Simmons seemed to bother Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold all night. “According to Next Gen Stats, the Seahawks were held to 3.0 yards per play (3 sacks, INT) in the 48 plays where Simmons was on the field. In the eight plays where he was off the field, Seattle averaged 13.3 yards per play,” ESPN reported. Seattle is looking to win another Super Bowl this season. This type of performance certainly won’t help them in the weeks moving forward. The Seahawks will now try to regroup. The team next plays the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. Seattle is now 4-4 on the year. Related: What Seahawks’ Sam Darnold said after stinking it up against Jeffery Simmons-led Bears pressure Related: Ref pool report explains 3 controversial plays that went against Seahawks vs. Bears

item.title: Goalkeeper Owono breaks down after collision that led to footballer’s death
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono was reportedly left distraught and broke down in tears in the dressing room after the accidental collision that preceded the death of CD Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel Alameda, with teammates rallying around him to offer support. According to The Sun UK, the 25-year-old Equatorial Guinea international was seen praying and crying following the incident during Monday’s Segunda División match between Tenerife and Andorra. Owono’s knee struck De Miguel’s head and chest as he rushed out to clear a long ball in the closing stages of the encounter. The 30-year-old striker was left motionless on the pitch, prompting distress among players, some of whom were reportedly seen in tears. The goalkeeper was shown a straight red card before the referee abandoned the match in second-half stoppage time. De Miguel was taken to hospital after reportedly suffering a cardiac arrest on the way, with paramedics said to have resuscitated him. Tenerife initially described his condition as “stable but serious” on Monday night, but he died on Tuesday morning. The Sun, citing Spanish newspaper AS, reported that Andorra players showed great concern for Owono during their journey back from Tenerife, with the goalkeeper visibly shaken by the tragedy. Journalist Ivan Alvarez also told COPE radio that Owono had intended to apologise to De Miguel’s family in person before learning of his death. The goalkeeper has reportedly deactivated his social media accounts since the incident and is said to be seeking an opportunity to offer his condolences to the bereaved family before making a public statement. Meanwhile, a judge is expected to open an investigation into De Miguel’s death, although a Canary Islands court source described the incident as an “accidental collision on the playing field”. The source explained that a judicial investigation is automatically opened in cases of deaths not resulting from natural causes, including accidents. Owono is not expected to face criminal sanctions, according to the report, although he could still face sporting disciplinary action. De Miguel’s partner, Maria, and their one-year-old daughter, Carla, were reportedly watching from the stands when the incident occurred. Tenerife have expressed their grief over the striker’s death, while UEFA has announced that a moment of silence will be observed at all its matches this week in his memory. Vanguard News The post Goalkeeper Owono breaks down after collision that led to footballer’s death appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Mizzou’s 9-3 Record Could Still Land A Playoff Spot
item.description: Denny Medley-Imagn Images A 9-3 record usually means a team goes home early, but the Missouri Tigers might be the exception this year. The 19th-ranked Tigers defeated Arkansas 34-10 on Halloween night in Fayetteville to improve their season to 6-2. While a three-loss finish often disqualifies a team from the College Football Playoff, a new survey from SBN Reacts asks fans if Mizzou can still make the cut with that exact record. The answer depends on how they handle a brutal final stretch of games. A Gauntlet of Ranked Teams Per Rock M Nation , Missouri faces the second toughest remaining schedule in the entire country according to reports. The Tigers must host No. 10 Texas, travel to No. 2 Georgia, play at home against No. 8 Kentucky, and finish against Oklahoma. These four games alone decide if the season ends in a bowl game or a playoff berth. There is almost no room for error after losing to Mississippi State and Ole Miss earlier in the year. Penalties Cost Big Gains Even when the team plays well, self-inflicted wounds often hurt the final result. Caleb Goodie Sr. nullified a 16-yard gain by Jamal Roberts via a holding penalty during the recent victory against Arkansas. Offense momentum stalled as the squad finished with nine penalties totaling 80 yards. Head coach Eliah Drinkwitz admitted the struggle in his postgame comments. “Offensively, we were just continually stubbing our toes with penalties,” Drinkwitz said. “We’ve got to get that cleaned up. In the second half, we were much better.” Despite the penalty issues, the offense found new ways to move the ball. Quarterback Austin Simmons and wide receiver DeMarion Fowlkes used jet sweeps and designed runs to keep the defense guessing. Muscling through for a six-yard gain on a jet sweep, the 5-foot-9 receiver Fowlkes executed just one cut before the play concluded. This unique play call helped the Tigers secure a 13-0 lead before halftime and eventually win the game. The coaching staff used these east-west plays to generate quick touches for their best players. Running Backs Lead the Charge Jamal Roberts carried the ball 23 times for 138 yards and one touchdown against Arkansas. This performance pushed his season total past 1,000 rushing yards, making him the 53rd player in program history to reach that mark. He currently leads the entire Power Four conference with 1,005 rushing yards through eight games. The defense also stepped up when it mattered most on Saturday night. Junior linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez made nine total tackles and forced a fumble to help secure the victory. Safety Trajen Greco added eight tackles, an interception, and a pass deflection to stop Arkansas drives. Greco now has three interceptions on the year, which ties for second in the SEC. These individual efforts show why Mizzou has won five straight games in the Battle Line Rivalry. The question remains whether the team can survive the final four games to reach nine wins. These four games alone decide if the season ends in a bowl game or a playoff berth. There is almost no room for error after losing to Mississippi State and Ole Miss earlier in the year. Penalties Cost Big Gains Even when the team plays well, self-inflicted wounds often hurt the final result. Caleb Goodie Sr. nullified a 16-yard gain by Jamal Roberts via a holding penalty during the recent victory against Arkansas. Offense momentum stalled as the squad finished with nine penalties totaling 80 yards. Head coach Eliah Drinkwitz admitted the struggle in his postgame comments. “Offensively, we were just continually stubbing our toes with penalties,” Drinkwitz said. “We’ve got to get that cleaned up. In the second half, we were much better.” Despite the penalty issues, the offense found new ways to move the ball. Quarterback Austin Simmons and wide receiver DeMarion Fowlkes used jet sweeps and designed runs to keep the defense guessing. Muscling through for a six-yard gain on a jet sweep, the 5-foot-9 receiver Fowlkes executed just one cut before the play concluded. This unique play call helped the Tigers secure a 13-0 lead before halftime and eventually win the game. The coaching staff used these east-west plays to generate quick touches for their best players. Running Backs Lead the Charge Jamal Roberts carried the ball 23 times for 138 yards and one touchdown against Arkansas. This performance pushed his season total past 1,000 rushing yards, making him the 53rd player in program history to reach that mark. He currently leads the entire Power Four conference with 1,005 rushing yards through eight games. The defense also stepped up when it mattered most on Saturday night. Junior linebacker Nicholas Rodriguez made nine total tackles and forced a fumble to help secure the victory. Safety Trajen Greco added eight tackles, an interception, and a pass deflection to stop Arkansas drives. Greco now has three interceptions on the year, which ties for second in the SEC. These individual efforts show why Mizzou has won five straight games in the Battle Line Rivalry. The question remains whether the team can survive the final four games to reach nine wins. If they do, the College Football Playoff committee may have to look at the strength of their schedule rather than just the loss column. The fans will have their say in the weekly SBN Reacts survey about this exact possibility.

item.content:encoded: IOWA CITY, IOWA- OCTOBER 26: Running back Kamari Moulton #28 of the Iowa Hawkeyes runs through a hole during the first half against the Northwestern Wildcats at Kinnick Stadium on October 26, 2024 in Iowa City, Iowa. (Photo by Matthew Holst/Getty Images) | Getty Images Well, that’s more like it. One week after handing away the pig in Minneapolis, the Hawkeyes took out every ounce of frustration on #25 Wisconsin in a 30-0 shutout that kept the Heartland Trophy in Iowa City for a fifth straight year. The dominant performance also put Iowa back in the AP poll at #21 and the Coaches Poll at #20. Hank Brown was surgical in his return to the lineup (20-of-24 for 222 yards and two scores. The performance was good enough to win Big Ten Offensive Player of the Week (when is the last time Iowa had their QB win that award?). He spread the ball around to 7 different receivers with DJ Vonnahme, Reece Vander Zee and Tony Diaz all topping 50 yards on the day. The defense allowed just 52 rushing yards and nine first downs and the one-week character check came back emphatic. The reward is a genuinely fascinating road trip. Iowa heads to Evanston to take on Northwestern on Saturday night (6:30 pm CT on FOX) for its first look at the new Ryan Field. The roughly $870 million, 35,000-seat palace on the lakefront opened a month ago and bills itself as the most expensive college football stadium ever built. Despite the smaller size, it’s still a haven for visiting fans. Tickets for this weekend’s matchup are largely in line with the cost to buy season tickets to the Wildcats. Both teams enter the week at 6-2 overall and 3-2 in Big Ten play. Both have been ranked in recent weeks, but it’s Iowa now moving up after the big win over the Badgers while Northwestern finds themselves just outside the top-25 this week after falling on the road ta Oregon last Saturday. Despite the loss, FanDuel Sportsbook has Northwestern favored by 1.5 in this one with an over/under of 44.5 total points. So Iowa is a road dog to a team it has beaten four straight times, with an implied final somewhere around 23-21. The books are telling you this Northwestern team is different. And they may have a case. A Different Northwestern The David Braun rebuild is fully realized now. Four years after taking over as the interim HC, he’s won two bowls, banked a Big Ten Coach of the Year award, signed an extension through 2031 and built a 6-2 team whose only losses are one-score road games at Indiana and Oregon. There are no bad losses on the resume. There’s also a distinctly Iowa-flavored footnote: Braun cut his teeth on Northern Iowa’s staff before his NDSU years, so he knows exactly what kind of football is coming Saturday. The biggest change this year is on offense, where Northwestern handed the play sheet to Chip Kelly. He inherited Michigan State transfer Aidan Chiles and has turned him into one of the most efficient quarterbacks in the conference. Chiles is completing 68.8% of his passes for 1,898 yards with 13 touchdowns and only single interception, plus 10 more scores on the ground. Caleb Komolafe (618 yards) and Joseph Himon II (8.9 a carry) power a rushing attack ranked 24th nationally, and SDSU transfer Griffin Wilde (44-761-5) is a legitimate WR1. They convert 46.5% of their third downs. This is not the 12-points-a-game Northwestern of recent memory – it’s a top top-35 scoring offense (33.6 PPG) and a top-30 total offense (438.1 yards per game). The flip side is a defense that will statistically be the worst Iowa has faced since the opener. The Wildcats rank 84th in total defense, 75th against the run, 94th against the pass and tied for 100th in sacks with 13 all season. Northwestern seems to have taken a page out of the Phil Parker book and is seemingly happy to give up yardage as long as they can hold opponents to FGs. While the Wildcats rank poorly on yards allowed, they remain top-25 in scoring defense, giving up 18.75 points per game thanks to the 16th best red zone defense (tied with Iowa). Northwestern is holding opponents to a FG or scoreless on 57% of their red zone trips. The Matchup Stat to Watch Turnover margin: Northwestern is +10, fifth in the country. Iowa is +1. Everything about Iowa’s season (and frankly, the KF tenure) says that column decides the outcome Saturday. The Minneapolis loss featured four giveaways all by itself while the wins have been built on clean football and a defense that ranks 4th nationally in both points allowed (12.5) and rushing yards allowed (79.0). Chiles has thrown just one interception in eight games and Phil Parker’s unit has to be the one that finally makes him flinch. The pass rush is tied for 11th nationally with 24 sacks and is facing an offense that has barely turned it over all year, making this the chess match of the night. On the other side, Iowa’s offense gets the most forgiving matchup it has seen since the trip to Seattle. An offensive line that has spent the season among the nation’s stingiest in sacks allowed faces a front with 13 all year. Xavier Williams and L.J. Phillips face the 75th-ranked run defense and the Hawkeyes will have to be able to run the ball. If Iowa’s 70th-ranked scoring offense can’t find the mid-20s against this group, it’s an answer about the offense, not the opponent. Last week, more than 60% of the community thought we already had that question answered against Minnesota. The Wisconsin performance likely shifts the view, but falling flat again this week against a mediocre Northwestern team would seem to indicate Wisconsin was the anomaly, not Minnesota. Here’s a quick look at the details for Saturday’s matchup. Date: Saturday, November 7 Time: 6:30 pm CT Matchup: #21 Iowa Hawkeyes (6-2, 3-2) at Northwestern Wildcats (6-2, 3-2) Location: Ryan Field, Evanston, Illinois TV: FOX Initial Weather Forecast: Mostly cloudy, game-time temps in the upper 40s with light wind off the lake FanDuel Opening Line : Northwestern -1.5 O/U 44.5 Series History Iowa leads this series by nearly 30 games all-time, thanks in large part to a 21-game winning streak from 1974 to 1994. The Hawkeyes are trying to start another long streak, having won the last four and six of the last ten. The Wildcats are no longer a doormat, though, so expecting this streak to last too terribly long is a fool’s dream. The two team’s didn’t face off last year and last saw each other in 2024 when the Hawkeyes won 40-14. The 2023 meeting came in Wrigley Field (Iowa won 10-7), so the Hawkeyes haven’t played in Evanston since the current streak started back in 2021 when Iowa won 17-12. Northwestern hasn’t beaten Iowa at home since 2017 and head coach Ryan Braun is 0-2 against Kirk Ferentz. No trophy changes hands in this one, but the calendar supplies some unique history. Saturday is November 7, marking 17 years to the day since unranked Northwestern walked into Kinnick and stunned a 9-0 Iowa team that sat #4 in the BCS standings, 17-10, after Ricky Stanzi went down with an ankle injury Different era of Northwestern football, same lesson: this program has enjoys ruining great Iowa seasons.

item.title: Politano: ‘Napoli are fragile at the moment, but no alibi against Porto’
item.description: Politano: ‘Napoli are fragile at the moment, but no alibi against Porto’ Matteo Politano admits Napoli are ‘fragile’ defensively and concede too easily, but mustn’t ‘use injuries as an alibi’ for the Champions League trip to FC Porto. It kicks off at the Estadio do Dragao on Wednesday at 20.00 GMT (21.00 CET). The Partenopei are playing catch-up in the tournament after one win and two defeats, but that is still better than their opponents, who lost all three matches so far in the Champions League. Max Allegri’s side also stumbled in Serie A at the weekend, losing 2-0 away to Juventus. Politano sees Napoli problems NAPLES, ITALY – OCTOBER 20: Matteo Politano of SSC Napoli celebrates scoring his team’s first goal during the UEFA Champions League 2026/27 League Phase MD3 match between SSC Napoli and FK Bodo/Glimt at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on October 20, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) “A difficult game awaits us tomorrow. It’s true that we have some injuries, but this mustn’t be used as an alibi, we don’t want alibis at this moment,” said Politano in his press conference. “We are the only ones who can drag ourselves out of this situation. We’ve got to give our all on the pitch, because this is a fundamental match for us.” NAPLES, ITALY – APRIL 06: Matteo Politano of SSC Napoli celebrates after scoring the opening goal during the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and AC Milan at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on April 06, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) The recurring problem for Napoli this season is how many goals they are conceding, and assistant manager Marco Landucci confirmed players backing off when defending is not something suggested by the coaching staff. “When we concede goals, it’s everyone’s fault and not just the defenders, this is a team sport,” confessed Politano. “We are fragile at the moment, we can’t seem to defend as well as we did in previous years. We lack determination in pressing the opponents, so naturally against quality players you are going to pay for that. “We’ve got to come together as a unit and try from tomorrow to be more solid. We haven’t tested the line-up yet, so we don’t know if it’ll be three or four at the back, but it is no problem for me.” ITALY – OCTOBER 28: Matteo Politano of SSC Napoli celebrates after scoring team’s second goal during the Serie A match between AC Monza and SSC Napoli at U-Power Stadium on October 28, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Pier Marco Tacca/Getty Images) Napoli fumbled a lead for the 3-1 Champions League defeat to Villarreal , and Politano made a very costly error with a howler of a back-pass. “Unfortunately, we can do nothing about the past, we need to focus on the future,” added the winger. “I challenge myself every single day to give more, I’ve won a lot with this team, but I’ve got to keep pushing. It’s not an easy situation, we’ve all got to come together and stay concentrated at all times. “Porto are a strong si

item.title: Rumor Opens Door For NY Giants & Philadelphia Eagles Blockbuster Trade, But It’s Not For Saquon Barkley
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect A new NFL trade rumor opens the door for the New York Giants to address a major need in a deal with rivals, the Philadelphia Eagles , before next week’s deadline. The Giants and Eagles head into the Week 9 NFL schedule in very different positions. New York has been one of the feel-good stories in the NFL this season, because despite losing their starting quarterback and top pass rusher, they sit atop the NFC East with a 4-2-1 record. On the flip side, injuries — especially to Jalen Hurts — have had a far bigger effect on Philadelphia’s 2-6 record over the first half of the season. Ahead of the Nov. 10 trade deadline, reports point to the Giants being buyers, while the Eagles could be big sellers. But could the two NFC East teams actually work together on a deal? With New York allegedly looking to upgrade the running back spot, a trade for Saquon Barkley seems intriguing. It would give them the elite back they want, while righting the wrong of letting him leave Big Blue for Philly in free agency two years ago. However, recent reports claim the Eagles have informed the three-time Pro Bowler that they have no plans to move him. NFL insider Jason LaCanfora backed up that belief in a Tuesday report when he suggested Barkley is near untouchable. But there is a different star who would address a Giants need and might be up for grabs before the deadline. Should the New York Giants pursue a Jalen Carter trade? Oct 11, 2026; Tottenham, ENG; Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jalen Carter (98) reacts during the second half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images “Executives have also long wondered whether the Eagles would be able to retain both former first-round defensive tackle selections, Jordan Davis and Jalen Carter . But Philadelphia won’t sell low on either if a deal presents itself,” LaCanfora wrote. The word around the NFL is that the Giants are trying to find upgrades at running back and the interior of their defensive line after trading Dexter Lawrence in the offseason. The two-time Pro Bowler would absolutely fill that void. Furthermore, the 25-year-old is also under contract for five more seasons . The big question is what would the price be? The Giants got the 10th overall pick in April’s draft for Lawrence, who is a three-time Pro Bowler and only three years older than Carter. It is possible the Eagles ask for a first-rounder plus a future Day 3 pick for the talented defensive tackle. Do you think the G-Men would be willing to pay that price? item.title: Blue Jays Cut Ties With Gold Glover After Just Two Seasons
item.description: Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Myles Straw One year after winning the American League and coming two outs away from winning the World Series, the Toronto Blue Jays missed the postseason entirely this year. Some stars underperforming and injuries held the Blue Jays back, despite the team taking an aggressive approach in free agency. This offseason is a very important one for the Blue Jays as they look to get back into October in a stacked American League East. The team has already started making some roster moves as free agency begins, and one of the moves they made was declining Myles Straw's $8 million club option, making him a free agent. Straw won a Gold Glove Award with the Cleveland Guardians in 2022 as a center fielder. The Blue Jays acquired him in a trade in 2025. In the last two seasons, he has played all three outfield spots, but has spent most of his time in left field and center field. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! Offensively, he posted a .662 OPS in the last two seasons. Even though his OPS was not great, he posted a .262 batting average in 2025, proving he could at least be a consistent force getting on base. This year, his batting average and on-base percentage both dropped. Simply put, he did not play like a player worth $8 million. The Blue Jays gave him a $1.75 million buyout, and adding a quality outfielder will be a huge focus for the team. There are already reports that they are interested in Seiya Suzuki. He would be a huge upgrade for their outfield. More MLB: Mets Reportedly Cooling On Japanese Slugger Teruaki Sato For This Reason

item.title: ‘I threw that cup in the trash’: Fan reacts after LeBron James sips his wine
item.description: Oct 20, 2026; New York, New York, USA; Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James (23) on the court before the start of the second quarter against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images LeBron James has never hidden his love of wine. On Monday night, he got an unexpected taste in the middle of a game. While chasing a loose ball during the Philadelphia 76ers’ win over the Chicago Bulls, James crashed into a fan holding a cup of red wine. So he grabbed the cup and took a sip before heading back onto the court. LeBron Drinks Fan’s Wine James has been off to a strong start in his first season in Philadelphia. The 76ers improved to 7-1 with a 126-107 win over the Bulls on Monday, and James finished with 15 points, seven rebounds, and nine assists. However, it was an incident that happened in the stands that stole the headlines. During the third quarter, with the 76ers up by 11. James collided with the fan while chasing the ball out of bounds, then took a sip from his cup, as seen in video of the moment . After the game, James explained what happened. “I spilled some of his wine. I crashed into him, spilled some of his wine. So I wanted to see if it was worth it on my arm and how good it was. It was all right,” James said, via ESPN’s Kris Rhim . ‘I Threw That Cup in the Trash’ The fan, longtime Sixers season-ticket holder Troy Clemons, wasn’t upset about it, either. “I’m just glad for him to be here,” Clemons told ESPN . “I’m not worried about the wine getting on me.” Rhim also asked Clemons what he did with the cup James drank from. Clemons didn’t keep it as a souvenir. “At the end of the day, he’s another man like me. I mean, he’s LeBron. But at the end of the day, I threw that cup in the trash,” Clemons said. He added that he didn’t mean any disrespect by it. “It’s nothing up with him. I just got a fresh drink, though,” Clemons said. Needless to say, it’s a moment he won’t forget anytime soon, even if he didn’t save the cup. The post ‘I threw that cup in the trash’: Fan reacts after LeBron James sips his wine appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

Needless to say, it’s a moment he won’t forget anytime soon, even if he didn’t save the cup. item.title: Jon Rahm Rejects LIV 2.0, Eyes PGA Tour Return
item.description: Jerod Ringwald-Imagn Images The two-time Major winner turned down an offer to stay with the LIV Golf League under its new 2.0 structure. He told reporters that the revised plan simply did not feel right for his career path. This decision comes as the tour navigates a shift in leadership and financial backing. Rahm is now looking toward a potential return to the PGA Tour while serving a suspension. The Spanish star made these comments during his pre‑tournament press conference. The tournament will be his first official start on the DP World Tour since leaving the Saudi-backed circuit. He reflected on his time away, noting that while he enjoyed the experience, the future direction of the league was not inspiring. He told reporters, “Well, I would say I can only reflect on those three years as a positive. It was a wonderful experience. Played a lot of good golf. Obviously individually and as a team, we did great.” Despite the success he found in the team format, the changes proposed for LIV 2.0 were a dealbreaker. As reported by Yahoo News Singapore , Rahm explained that he “wasn’t thrilled with the changes they were doing to 2.0 and I just wasn’t willing to follow that path.” He felt the league was moving away from what made it unique and becoming too much like a regular tour. The exit of the Saudi PIF as backers has left the league in flux, with new creditors BC Partners attempting to launch a second iteration in 2027. Rahm noted there were “too many unknowns at the time” regarding the commitment deadline. He felt the proposal lacked the special qualities that defined the original concept. His focus has now shifted to the PGA Tour, though a formal return has not been finalized. Rahm revealed he has not yet had a conversation with the tour about his reinstatement. He told the press, “As of right now, I really don’t know what 2027 is going to look like for me.” Earlier in the year, the PGA Tour offered a deal similar to the one Brooks Koepka accepted, which involved a $5 million donation to charity and restrictions on sponsor exemptions. Rahm, along with Bryson DeChambeau and Cameron Smith, did not agree to those terms by the deadline. The tour has since gone silent on the matter, leaving the timing of his return uncertain. The Path Forward for the Spaniard Rahm’s rejection of the LIV 2.0 offer signals a preference for the traditional tour model. He valued the team aspect of LIV 1.0 but could not accept the diluted vision of the new version. His comments suggest a player who prioritizes the competitive integrity of the game over the potential for a massive, albeit uncertain, payout from a restructured league. The financial incentives of the PGA Tour Champions or a new LIV deal did not sway him when the core product changed. He continues to compete on the DP World Tour while awaiting a decision on his PGA Tour reinstatement. Rahm chose to wait rather than accept a compromised deal. He is willing to play on the DP World Tour while the PGA Tour decides

item.title: DeForest Buckner gets his old number back
item.description: Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Not that it was ever a mystery, DeForest Buckner’s return to the San Francisco 49ers means he’s getting his old No. 99 back. That number has been worn by second-year defensive tackle CJ West. Buckner said he got to know West last week and the two were talking, where West told Buckner, “Hey, bro, 99 is yours.” West will wear No. 90. Buckner didn’t need to ask for the number. He said West offered it to him. Buckner vowed to “take care” of West, even though CJ asked for nothing in return. Buckner denied telling the Colts he only wanted to be traded to the 49ers. He also wouldn’t say whether he’s discussed or focused on a potential extension with the 49ers after this season. His focus is on the remainder of the season. “Fred and I were just talking in the cafe this morning. You really wanna be a team on the rise. This is a part of the season where, you know, some teams start falling off. The really select group continues to rise and get better every week. That’s what I’m doing. That’s what I’m trying to do.” During Buckner’s press conference on Monday, he said some of his new teammates told him Kris Kocurek plays a lot of 2019 film as teaching tape. The nostalgia is great, but the 49ers brought in Buckner to do a job and do it at a high level. He said he plans to do everything he can to help elevate the defensive line room. When asked about the immediate impact he could make, Buckner leaned into his experience, but also wants to help the young players in the room: “There’s a lot of young guys in the room. I’m an open book. If they want to pick my brain and ask me questions, I’m always an open book to all of them. It doesn’t take just one or two guys to make a room or make a team. It’s the entire room. I’ve always believed that the d-line is the engine of the team. And I wanna pour into those young guys everything that I know, so I can help their game and get even better.” How the snaps look with Buckner in the fold is one of the more intriguing parts about the defense moving forward. Buckner still has the stamina to play 70-75% of the time. That means whoever is next to him will be rotated quite a bit to keep them fresh.

item.title: DSS DG frees four suspected IPOB members, pays N20m compensation
item.description: The Director-General of the Department of State Services (DGSS), Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi has set free and approved an initial payment of N20 million to four suspects, out of which, each suspect is to receive five million Naira as compensation after being cleared of alleged membership of the proscribed Indigenous People of Biafra (IPOB). Security sources disclosed that the suspects; Emele Uduma Ibe, Berefgagha Appah, Ondokeyilemi Aggry and Oyeinmokebebeton Aggry, were arrested in May 2022, in Sampou and Akeddei communities in Kolokuma/Opokuma and Sagbama Local Government Areas of Bayelsa State. “The Agency established that they had been misled into believing that they would each receive a monthly payment of N100,000 under the Federal Government’s Amnesty Programme, not knowing that they were being lured by a group of IPOB members who are now facing trial,” disclosed one of the sources. While receiving the four, Deji Adeyanju & Partners, Counsel to the suspects, commended the Service for their relentless efforts towards safeguarding Nigeria’s security, particularly acknowledging the DGSS’ genuine attempt at upholding human rights. Furthermore, he noted the high level of hygiene and professionalism within the Service, being the best he has witnessed in over 20 years of interacting with DSS personnel. He reiterated his earlier public statement that President Tinubu made the right choice in appointing Oluwatosin Adeola Ajayi as DSS DG. Expressing gratitude to the DSS boss, Emele Uduma Ibe who spoke on behalf of others, described the day as the happiest of his life, noting that the experience had taught him a valuable lesson which he would share with others. He offered prayers for God’s continued blessings upon the DSS boss and the management of the Service. Recall that upon assuming office in 2024, the DG ordered a review of over 300 inherited terrorism cases. Currently, the DSS panel has been able to decongest its facility to about 100 after thorough investigations, paying over a billion naira in compensation. The DSS boss awarded N20 million and covered the medical bills of a Jos based businessman, who was shot erroneously by service personnel in Plateau State. Chineze Ozoadibe was also compensated with N10 million after she was wrongfully arrested, Sunday Ifedi who was also compensated with 10 million naira after investigation cleared him of ties with IPOB, likewise Kenneth Okechukwu Nwafor was also paid N5 million after investigation absolved him of IPOB allegations. This is aside other numerous cases that the DSS has handled quietly which never made news outside the Agency. “Like other compensated suspects, the DSS will also offer psychological, medical support to these four in addition the initial amount given,” I’m confident the DSS will also help further reintegration into the society, revealed a source. The DG- DSS in a recent maiden media interview admitted that, as humans, the DSS is prone to mistakes. However, where there is injury, Mr Aja

item.title: 2027: Why youth share of voters dropped – INEC
item.description: ….As UniJos wins campus debate finale By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why youths now make up 29.79 per cent of the voters’ register being prepared for the 2027 general election, down from 39.65 per cent in the 2023 register. Chairman of the commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, gave the explanation on Tuesday at the grand finale of the INEC Campus Debate at the Law Theatre of the University of Abuja. He said the drop does not mean fewer young people are interested in elections, but that many who counted as youths in 2023 have simply grown older. “Some questions have been asked, why has the number reduced compared to what we have in 2023? But the truth of the matter is that there has been progressive migration of the categories of persons that were youth in 2023, they have now migrated into different age groups”, Amupitan explained. He said the register, “which is currently being reviewed through claims and objection,” puts youth representation at 29.79 per cent. The 2023 register had 37,060,399 youths aged 18 to 34, or 39.65 per cent of the 93.4 million registered voters. Amupitan said the debate was part of the commission’s effort to confront voter apathy among young people. “Our plan is to catch them young,” he said. He said earlier outings showed how little many young people know about the electoral process. “When they ask who is the INEC chairman, unfortunately none of them could get it,” he said. The University of Jos won the final, which was held under the theme “Nigeria’s Electoral Process and Democracy.” Bayero University, Kano, came second, the University of Ibadan third, and the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, fourth. Amupitan, who is a University of Jos alumnus, said the judges’ decision could not be faulted. “From the quality of the debate, it was, honestly, it could go either way and they have done justice to it,” he said. He said the judges took a long time to compute the scores. “They were also trying to use technology with their phone making some computations and arithmetics just to ensure that there is accurate delivery,” he said. Amupitan said the result was so clear that no debater or university should think of going to court. “It will be needless for any of the parties or debaters to think of going to court. So that is why we are not establishing any election petition, any tribunal to review what has been done,” he said light-heartedly. item.content:encoded: ….As UniJos wins campus debate finale By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: The Independent National Electoral Commission INEC has explained why youths now make up 29.79 per cent of the voters’ register being prepared for the 2027 general election, down from 39.65 per cent in the 2023 register. Chairman of the commission, Prof. Joash Amupitan SAN, gave the explanation on Tuesday at the grand finale of the INEC Campus Debate at the Law Theatre of the University of Abuja. He said the drop does not mean fewer young people are interested in elections, but that many who counted as youths in 2023 have simply grown older. “Some questions have been asked, why has the number reduced compared to what we have in 2023? But the truth of the matter is that there has been progressive migration of the categories of persons that were youth in 2023, they have now migrated into different age groups”, Amupitan explained. He said the register, “which is currently being reviewed through claims and objection,” puts youth representation at 29.79 per cent. The 2023 register had 37,060,399 youths aged 18 to 34, or 39.65 per cent of the 93.4 million registered voters. Amupitan said the debate was part of the commission’s effort to confront voter apathy among young people. “Our plan is to catch them young,” he said. He said earlier outings showed how little many young people know about the electoral process. “When they ask who is the INEC chairman, unfortunately none of them could get it,” he said. The University of Jos won the final, which was held under the theme “Nigeria’s Electoral Process and Democracy.” Bayero University, Kano, came second, the University of Ibadan third, and the University of Nigeria, Nsukka, fourth. Amupitan, who is a University of Jos alumnus, said the judges’ decision could not be faulted. “From the quality of the debate, it was, honestly, it could go either way and they have done justice to it,” he said. He said the judges took a long time to compute the scores. “They were also trying to use technology with their phone making some computations and arithmetics just to ensure that there is accurate delivery,” he said. Amupitan said the result was so clear that no debater or university should think of going to court. “It will be needless for any of the parties or debaters to think of going to court. So that is why we are not establishing any election petition, any tribunal to review what has been done,” he said light-heartedly. He also told the Director of Voter Education and Publicity to keep track of the finalists, saying he would have employed them immediately if the law allowed. “They are not qualified to have been given automatic employment, if not I will have done that by now,” he said. He added that they must first graduate and complete the National Youth Service Corps NYSC. He noted that a debater from Bayero University, Kano, studies medicine, while the two debaters from the University of Jos study law. The INEC chairman told the audience that elections under his watch have shown improvement. “I am just one year 10 days in office,” he said, adding that the commission had conducted four off-cycle elections: the Anambra governorship election, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) area council elections in February, the Ekiti governorship election in June and the Osun governorship election in August. “Go back to history, Anambra election and Osun election used to be inconclusive. But under our watch, we have ensured to a large extent that those elections are conclusive”, he said. On women’s participation, he said the commission has a gender and inclusivity department. He noted that Belgium requires equality in the occupation of political offices, “but we don’t have such a law in Nigeria yet.” To the finalists, he said: “You have spoken with conviction, with candor and with discipline.” The Vice Chancellor of the University of Abuja, Professor Hakeem Babatunde Fawehinmi, urged young Nigerians to collect their voter cards, turn out to vote and hold leaders accountable. He commended INEC for the initiative and said debate teaches young people to manage disagreement. “It can be argued that debate is the opposite of violence,” he said. item.title: Tenerife footballer Jesús de Miguel dies aged 30 after on-pitch collision
item.description: Police homicide division opens judicial proceedings He was struck in the chest when challenging for ball Spanish football was in shock on Tuesday after the Tenerife striker Jesús de Miguel died after a collision with the Andorra goalkeeper Jesús Owono during a match in the second division. The homicide division of the national police has opened judicial proceedings into a possible involuntary manslaughter, a routine procedure after any death not by natural causes. The chief public prosecutor in Santa Cruz de Tenerife told the state news agency EFE that it was “very difficult” for a case to come to court. Tenerife announced that De Miguel had died at 8am on Tuesday after he had been taken into intensive care on Monday afternoon. He did not regain consciousness after a cardiorespiratory arrest. Continue reading...

item.title: The Xbox Nano has a hidden cloud secret
item.description: Microsoft is about to launch its new Xbox Nano controller tomorrow, and the tiny device has a little secret. The Nano can connect directly to Xbox Cloud Gaming over Wi-Fi to improve latency. item.title: Police uncover fake dollar operation in Ondo, arrest suspect
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Police Command has uncovered a suspected counterfeit dollar printing operation in Odigbo Local Government Area, arresting one suspect and recovering three bags of suspected fake United States dollar notes. The operation followed an investigation into an alleged $6,000 currency fraud involving a businessman in Okitipupa. The police said the case began after Yusuf Nasiru, of Sabo, Okitipupa, lodged a complaint on October 28, 2026, alleging that two men, Peter Desmond and Olami Toro, both from Ode-Irele, approached him at his shop on October 25 to exchange dollars for naira. According to the complainant, he handed over $6,000, valued at about N8.6 million, to the men. However, while waiting for the naira equivalent, the suspects allegedly returned the dollars, claiming they did not have enough money to complete the transaction, before leaving. Nasiru later discovered that the returned notes were counterfeit and reported the matter to the police. The Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Jimoh Abayomi, said operatives of the Okitipupa Division commenced an investigation following receipt of the complaint. He said intelligence gathering and technical tracking led the operatives to one of the suspects, Peter Desmond, at Kiniso Village, via Ajue, in Odigbo LGA. “Acting on credible intelligence from community members, operatives raided the hideout on October 29, 2026, believed to be used for producing and printing counterfeit dollar notes to defraud unsuspecting members of the public,” Abayomi said. He disclosed that one suspect was arrested during the raid, while other occupants of the premises escaped through a perimeter fence. A search of the premises, he said, led to the recovery of three bags containing suspected counterfeit US dollar notes and a small wooden box, which had been taken into police custody as exhibits. Abayomi added that the arrested suspect had provided useful information to assist the ongoing investigation. He said the Commissioner of Police, Felix Ohagwu, had directed that the investigation be intensified to apprehend other suspects, establish the full extent of the alleged criminal network and prosecute those found culpable. The command cautioned residents against engaging in suspicious foreign currency transactions with unverified individuals or accepting seemingly attractive exchange offers outside authorised channels. It also advised members of the public to authenticate foreign currencies before accepting them and report suspicious activities to the nearest police station. The police assured residents of their commitment to combating financial crimes and protecting lives and property across the state. The post Police uncover fake dollar operation in Ondo, arrest suspect appeared first on Vanguard News .
