item.title: Nigeria’s exports rise 25% in two years — NPA
item.description: By Godwin Oritse The Nigerian Ports Authority (NPA) has said the country’s exports increased by more than 25 per cent in the last two years, attributing the growth to Federal Government reforms and improved collaboration with port operators. The Managing Director of NPA, Dr Abubakar Dantsoho, disclosed this while speaking at the ongoing Annual World Ports Conference in London, organised by the International Association of Ports and Harbours (IAPH). He said Nigeria’s population and economic potential gave it an advantage over other countries in West and Central Africa, adding that recent reforms had also improved cargo throughput at the nation’s ports. Dantsoho said the export growth was not limited to oil and gas but extended to manufacturing and agricultural products, including cocoa, cashew and other raw materials. “Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. And then these are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In terms of oil and gas, like I mentioned, we are doing fantastically around that, but then also in the other areas of manufacturing and agriculture, you know, raw materials like cocoa, like cashew and all that. Volumes have increased,” he said. He attributed the growth partly to the partnership between the NPA and major terminal operators, particularly APM Terminals. The NPA chief said the authority had put measures in place to sustain the growth, including the establishment of Export Processing Terminals to facilitate the handling and documentation of export cargoes. He disclosed that about four such terminals were operating in Nigeria, with the NPA collaborating with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargoes were processed locally and met required standards before shipment. Dantsoho said the reforms had also positioned Nigeria to take greater advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), particularly through increased trade with other African countries. He cited Nigeria’s engagement with Morocco, which he described as a growing manufacturing hub for electric and other vehicles, as an example of opportunities for cooperation. He said Nigeria’s population and economic potential gave it an advantage over other countries in West and Central Africa, adding that recent reforms had also improved cargo throughput at the nation’s ports. Dantsoho said the export growth was not limited to oil and gas but extended to manufacturing and agricultural products, including cocoa, cashew and other raw materials. “Statistically, the exports from Nigeria in the last two years has increased by 25 per cent. And then these are exports that are not mainly only oil and gas. In terms of oil and gas, like I mentioned, we are doing fantastically around that, but then also in the other areas of manufacturing and agriculture, you know, raw materials like cocoa, like cashew and all that. Volumes have increased,” he said. He attributed the growth partly to the partnership between the NPA and major terminal operators, particularly APM Terminals. The NPA chief said the authority had put measures in place to sustain the growth, including the establishment of Export Processing Terminals to facilitate the handling and documentation of export cargoes. He disclosed that about four such terminals were operating in Nigeria, with the NPA collaborating with terminal operators, the Nigeria Customs Service and other relevant agencies to ensure that export cargoes were processed locally and met required standards before shipment. Dantsoho said the reforms had also positioned Nigeria to take greater advantage of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), particularly through increased trade with other African countries. He cited Nigeria’s engagement with Morocco, which he described as a growing manufacturing hub for electric and other vehicles, as an example of opportunities for cooperation. The NPA managing director also attributed Nigeria’s improved performance in global port rankings to increased efficiency, technology adoption and collaboration with industry stakeholders. He said two Nigerian ports featured among the top 20 in the latest World Bank global ports ranking. Dantsoho further disclosed that revenue generated from ports across the country had quadrupled, alongside an increase in cargo volumes. He said the authority was monitoring port performance across West and Central Africa through a regional dashboard, adding that the data showed improvements in Nigeria’s port efficiency as well as progress in countries such as Tanzania and Kenya. According to him, the NPA plans to sustain partnerships with major industry players in countries including Morocco and South Africa to improve port operations and regional trade. On infrastructure development, Dantsoho said the Federal Government was planning to invest $1 billion in the expansion and modernisation of Apapa Port as part of its medium- to long-term strategy. He said the project would require substantial private-sector participation, adding that the NPA was working with APM Terminals and other investors to mobilise the required capital. The authority was also pursuing technology partnerships to improve port operations, he said. Dantsoho disclosed that the NPA had partnered with a Singaporean firm to develop a single-window system, while discussions were ongoing with a company from Abu Dhabi to develop a port community system. He said the initiatives were expected to improve coordination among port stakeholders, simplify processes and enhance efficiency. item.title: Google dismantles botnet secretly running on 1.3 million Android TV boxes
item.description: Google's Threat Intelligence Group says it has shut down a massive botnet called x.cpe. At its height, x.cpe ran on more than 1.3 million Android TV devices, and unusually, these were Google-certified boxes. Google says its screening process missed the malware due to "obfuscation techniques" employed by Shenzhen-based Videostrong Technology. In a detailed blog post , the Threat Intelligence Group explains how the x.cpe botnet evolved quickly from a single-stage dropper into a modular three-stage malware platform that sold access to third parties. Manufacturers must have their devices certified if they want access to Google apps and branding, a process that is supposed to catch threats like this. However, Videostrong's compromised boxes, mostly sold under the MECOOL brand, evaded detection by using a backdoor to remotely install the malware after the devices were set up and online. After devices appeared online, a stub application called x.cpe or com.oemservice would phone home. This package did not have any malicious capabilities of its own, but it had the system-level permissions necessary to install malware modules at the operator's behest. It also disabled Play Protect, which would have otherwise flagged the silently installed packages as malicious. Read full article Comments

item.title: Ondo Amotekun arrests 301 suspects, deploys 1,200 officers
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The Ondo State Security Network Agency, codenamed Amotekun, says it arrested 301 suspected kidnappers and other criminals between August and October 2026. The State Commander, Chief Adetunji Adeleye, disclosed this while parading 15 suspects, including those allegedly involved in the abduction of a poultry farmer, Afolabi Ajayi, in Imafon community, Akure North Local Government Area, and the killing of a woman. Adeleye also announced the launch of Operation Laafia DanDan, a security initiative aimed at tackling criminal activities during the ember months and yuletide. He said the corps had secured the conviction of 27 suspects, who were either serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions attached to options of fines. “Across the board, within these months under review, we arrested 301 suspects. Out of these 301 suspects, we have secured conviction of 27 serving various jail terms or fulfilling conditions for those that have option of fine. “Using alternative dispute resolution on many cases, we were able to resolve 102 cases,” he said. Adeleye attributed the achievements to the support of Amotekun ambassadors across the 18 local government areas, intelligence officers, local task forces, vigilantes and personnel of the corps. He said the agency was winding down its previous operation to begin full deployment for the ember months, with intelligence-led surveillance across the state, particularly on major highways, in urban centres and forest reserves. According to him, the new operation will feature increased patrols by Amotekun Rangers in forests, as well as electronic and physical monitoring of identified crime-prone locations. “We have redesigned a scheme whereby we will have a different operation for this period to guarantee safety of lives and property in Ondo State and for those commuting. “We want to reassure the public that the state remains safe as we are determined to continue 24/7 patrol across all major roads, forest reserves and the metropolis,” he said. The commander disclosed that about 1,200 personnel would be deployed across the 18 local government areas, with particular attention to border communities and routes. He also presented a kidnap victim who was recently rescued without payment of ransom. Adeleye said the corps had commenced training and retraining of personnel on arrest procedures and prosecution, adding that suspects whose investigations had been concluded would be charged to court. On the 15 suspects paraded, he said four were arrested for alleged violations of the state’s anti-grazing law, two for breach of law and order, while nine were arrested in connection with kidnapping. He said three suspects linked to the abduction of poultry farmer Ajayi and the killing of the woman had been arrested, adding that they were identified by the victim and had allegedly confessed to the offences. Other suspects, according to him, included individuals linked to a kidnapping incident in Ore, Ondo State

item.title: Okorocha to Uzodimma: Stop insulting judges, appeal up to the Supreme Court
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — A former governor of Imo State, Rochas Okorocha, whom the court recently declared the authentic candidate of the All Progressives Congress (APC) for the 2027 senatorial election in Imo West, has warned his successor, Governor Hope Uzodimma, to stop what he described as unwarranted attacks on judges. Okorocha, who spoke at the Federal High Court premises in Abuja after signing processes at the registry in connection with the ongoing legal dispute over the senatorial ticket, urged Governor Uzodimma to exercise his right of appeal, even up to the Supreme Court. He also called on the governor to restrain his supporters, whom he accused of continuing to denigrate the judiciary over a lost case. He said: “I listened to the news yesterday and it was so horrible, so terrible, that Governor Hope’s aides, namely his Deputy Chief of Staff and the National Vice Chairman of the APC, could berate a judge, insult a judge. “To use his words, he said the judgment was rubbish and procured, and that the judge should go and look at himself in the mirror. I think that is terrible. And the other one, who is called his Deputy Chief of Staff and whose wife is even a judge, could be insulting the judge because of a judgment. “So, it means that whenever the judgment is for Hope, it is good, but whenever it is against him, the Judiciary is evil. “I think this is very uncivilized. I want him to caution his attack dogs and his people to refrain from insulting judges. It doesn’t represent this nation well, and I feel particularly hurt. “I was made to understand that he has called all his aides, commissioners and everybody to go on the attack. You see, they are doing all that. Can’t he wait patiently and try to get the appeal through? At least the Supreme Court is there. “So it is very shocking and very surprising. I don’t know what they expected: that the judge should have said that the election was held on the 16th for Hope, when the actual date is the 18th? “Or that he would have said that Hope emerged by consensus, which is not true? Or the paper signed only by the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) of Imo State and sent to the National Chairman, saying that it was by consensus and that Hope’s election took place two days before the time? “I don’t understand what their quarrel is all about. I want to say once more: let us protect the sanctity of the Judiciary and let us allow justice to prevail in all matters. He said: “I listened to the news yesterday and it was so horrible, so terrible, that Governor Hope’s aides, namely his Deputy Chief of Staff and the National Vice Chairman of the APC, could berate a judge, insult a judge. “To use his words, he said the judgment was rubbish and procured, and that the judge should go and look at himself in the mirror. I think that is terrible. And the other one, who is called his Deputy Chief of Staff and whose wife is even a judge, could be insulting the judge because of a judgment. “So, it means that whenever the judgment is for Hope, it is good, but whenever it is against him, the Judiciary is evil. “I think this is very uncivilized. I want him to caution his attack dogs and his people to refrain from insulting judges. It doesn’t represent this nation well, and I feel particularly hurt. “I was made to understand that he has called all his aides, commissioners and everybody to go on the attack. You see, they are doing all that. Can’t he wait patiently and try to get the appeal through? At least the Supreme Court is there. “So it is very shocking and very surprising. I don’t know what they expected: that the judge should have said that the election was held on the 16th for Hope, when the actual date is the 18th? “Or that he would have said that Hope emerged by consensus, which is not true? Or the paper signed only by the Resident Electoral Commissioner (REC) of Imo State and sent to the National Chairman, saying that it was by consensus and that Hope’s election took place two days before the time? “I don’t understand what their quarrel is all about. I want to say once more: let us protect the sanctity of the Judiciary and let us allow justice to prevail in all matters. Hope has been a very big and unusual beneficiary of the court, and I think he should have respected it.” Okorocha challenged Uzodimma to fault his claims in public rather than attacking judges and the Judiciary, adding: “If you (Uzodimma) think any of the things I am saying is not true and that the judgment is not true, Hope should come on television or come and speak. “Why is he (Uzodimma) hiding and using attack dogs here and there to attack judges? That is very bad, and that shows what it means.” While accusing Governor Uzodimma of allegedly presenting forged documents during the hearing of the case, Okorocha expressed optimism that he would also win at the appellate court. He said: “In fact, if you look at the documents certified by INEC, according to Hope, and look at the inconsistencies and irregularities, then you could say that even the judge has no choice. Even a judge who wants to do wrong cannot do wrong in this case.” He also hailed the judiciary, which he said had served justice in the matter. “I salute the Nigerian Judiciary, honestly. Whatever you might say, they’re still very good. And I believe that the right thing should be done.” It will be recalled that the Federal High Court in Abuja on October 29 nullified the emergence of Governor Uzodimma as candidate of the APC for the Imo West Senatorial election slated for January 16, 2027. The court, in a judgment delivered by Justice Obiora Egwuatu, held that evidence before it established that Governor Uzodimma was not the valid winner of the primary election the APC conducted in the senatorial zone on May 18, which was monitored by INEC. According to the court, it was the former governor, Okorocha, who garnered the highest number of votes cast at the primary election and therefore ought to have been nominated by the party. Consequently, it ordered INEC to recognise Senator Okorocha forthwith and publish his name as the authentic candidate of the APC for the senatorial poll. The court further issued an order barring Governor Uzodimma from presenting himself as the candidate of the APC for the election. item.title: ‘The Cat in the Hat’ Review: Bill Hader Leads an Animated Dr. Seuss Comedy So Overstuffed It’s Like a Marvel Movie for Tots
item.description: The new "Cat in the Hat," it goes without saying at this point, makes no attempt to be a faithful adaptation of Dr. Seuss’s most fabled books. That would simply be too quaint for our buzzy, mercurial, attention-crashing, video-games-on-Ritalin era. Yet even as the movie departs all too eagerly from the innocent wildness of the Seuss books, it devotes itself, with a corporate diligence that’s the opposite of free-spirited, to mimicking the scale and spirit and plot setups of too many familiar blockbusters. It’s a mish-mosh of pop recycling.

item.content:encoded: The new "Cat in the Hat," it goes without saying at this point, makes no attempt to be a faithful adaptation of Dr. Seuss’s most fabled books. That would simply be too quaint for our buzzy, mercurial, attention-crashing, video-games-on-Ritalin era. Yet even as the movie departs all too eagerly from the innocent wildness of the Seuss books, it devotes itself, with a corporate diligence that’s the opposite of free-spirited, to mimicking the scale and spirit and plot setups of too many familiar blockbusters. It’s a mish-mosh of pop recycling.

item.title: D&D’s World of Warcraft Crossover Is the Bold Shake-Up the Game Needed
item.description: Wizards of the Coast has been playing things safe since updating the rules of Dungeons & Dragons 5th Edition in 2024. After lead designers Jeremy Crawford and Chris Perkins left Wizards in 2025 to join Critical Role ’s Darrington Press, Wizards slowed the pace of new D&D releases. Recent books have focused mostly on updating the lore and rules for the game’s most popular campaign settings and rebalancing previously published character options. D&D’s newest release bucks the trend, delivering an ambitious collection of innovative character options, monsters, and ways to use some of the game’s less developed subsystems. It just requires venturing to a new world.

item.title: Hubble Telescope sees cosmic 'cat's tail' that could wrap around Earth and the sun 500 times
item.description: null Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together. The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats. The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old , Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old. That means it is still host to collisions between planetary bodies similar to the ones that rocked the solar system during its infancy. The team behind this research gained new insights into the Cat's Tail using 14 years of observations. This allowed them to solve the long-standing mystery of the violent conditions under which it formed. "The Cat's Tail is thought to be the aftermath of a collision between large bodies — think something like Pluto ," team leader Arin Avsar of the University of Arizona said in a statement. "Oddly, this feature had previously only been seen with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), which detects infrared light, but remained invisible at shorter wavelengths, which has puzzled the community for a while." Cosmic cat tail is also pleasingly fluffy Comparing Beta Pictoris and our solar system, one thing rapidly becomes apparent: our cosmic neighborhood is relatively well-ordered. The planets orbit the sun with most space rocks neatly delegated into bands: the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter , and the Kuiper belt out beyond the orbit of Neptune. However, this is a stark contrast to the solar system's violent and chaotic youth. Back then, the solar system was host to an infant star surrounded by a swirling disk of gas and dust in which collisions between bodies called planetesimals — the building blocks of planets — were commonplace. Astronomers can't look back to the solar system's infancy, so to learn more about how our cosmic backyard took shape, they study nearby young planetary systems. Systems like Beta Pictoris. That doesn't mean it has been quick to divulge its secrets, though. "We think the Cat's Tail has eluded our observations in visible light until now because of what it's made of," Avsar explained. "It consists almost entirely of what we call organic refractory material, which is heavily carbon-based. These long chains of carbon atoms absorb visible light, so they're quite black." This new study revealed that the feline feature is cat-like in more ways than just its shape. It's also pleasingly fluffy, Hubble observations suggest. item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null Using the Hubble Space Telescope, astronomers have investigated a cosmic cat's tail, finding it likely formed after two Pluto-sized bodies smashed together. The feature, nicknamed the Cat's Tail, extends out from the debris disk known as Beta Pictoris which is located in a planetary system located 63 light-years away. This tail would put that of the average tabby to shame: It's so long that it could curl around the sun-Earth system about 500 times. That's about as long as 200 trillion house cats. The major difference between our solar system and the planetary system that hosts the Cat's Tail is the latter's relative youth. While our solar system is around 4.6 billion years old , Beta Pictoris is a cosmic kitten no more than a few million years old. That means it is still host to collisions between planetary bodies similar to the ones that rocked the solar system during its infancy. The team behind this research gained new insights into the Cat's Tail using 14 years of observations. This allowed them to solve the long-standing mystery of the violent conditions under which it formed. "The Cat's Tail is thought to be the aftermath of a collision between large bodies — think something like Pluto ," team leader Arin Avsar of the University of Arizona said in a statement. "Oddly, this feature had previously only been seen with the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST), which detects infrared light, but remained invisible at shorter wavelengths, which has puzzled the community for a while." Cosmic cat tail is also pleasingly fluffy Comparing Beta Pictoris and our solar system, one thing rapidly becomes apparent: our cosmic neighborhood is relatively well-ordered. The planets orbit the sun with most space rocks neatly delegated into bands: the main asteroid belt between Mars and Jupiter , and the Kuiper belt out beyond the orbit of Neptune. However, this is a stark contrast to the solar system's violent and chaotic youth. Back then, the solar system was host to an infant star surrounded by a swirling disk of gas and dust in which collisions between bodies called planetesimals — the building blocks of planets — were commonplace. Astronomers can't look back to the solar system's infancy, so to learn more about how our cosmic backyard took shape, they study nearby young planetary systems. Systems like Beta Pictoris. That doesn't mean it has been quick to divulge its secrets, though. "We think the Cat's Tail has eluded our observations in visible light until now because of what it's made of," Avsar explained. "It consists almost entirely of what we call organic refractory material, which is heavily carbon-based. These long chains of carbon atoms absorb visible light, so they're quite black." This new study revealed that the feline feature is cat-like in more ways than just its shape. It's also pleasingly fluffy, Hubble observations suggest. That's because the grains that compose it are extremely porous. "How you can get dust grains that small that are as porous as we see here no one really understands, and that's part of why we study this feature," Avsar said. "It's possible that the velocities involved in the collisions were so high that the carbon grains vaporized, turned into gas, and then recondensed as they cooled, and that's how they became so porous," team member Kevin Wagner of the U of A said. An illustration of the exoplanet Beta Pictoris b. (Image credit: NASA) The scientists also discovered a hitherto undiscovered feature in the Cat's Tail — a warp that seems to be the result of an interaction between the trail of material and one of the planets in the system, Beta Pictoris b, a gas giant planet 10 times more massive than Jupiter. "This gives us another line of evidence into how giant planets influence comets through their immense gravitational force," Avsar said. "It's a testament to how much these massive planets really influence their surrounding dust and icy bodies out to hundreds of astronomical units [one astronomical unit being the distance between Earth and the sun]." The team's research was published last month in The Astrophysical Journal Letters.

item.title: Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner
item.description: By Hadiza Yusuf The Kano State Government says clashes between farmers and herders have reduced significantly following the demarcation of 1,270 kilometres of cattle routes across the state. The Commissioner for Agriculture and Natural Resources, Dr Danjuma Mahmoud, disclosed this on Tuesday while outlining the achievements of the ministry. He said the demarcation had helped address recurring disputes between farmers and herders by providing designated routes for the movement of livestock. According to him, the initiative formed part of the state government’s efforts to tackle longstanding challenges in the agricultural sector and promote peaceful coexistence between farming and pastoral communities. “One important problem that I want to reiterate is the intractable problem of clashes between farmers and herders. We have made significant progress in that regard. “Our project provided demarcated cattle routes covering about 1,270 kilometres across the state. That is why you now hear that clashes between herders and farmers have reduced to the barest minimum in Kano State,” he said. Mahmoud said the ministry had also implemented interventions to boost agricultural production, including the rehabilitation of irrigation facilities and the expansion of cultivable farmland. He disclosed that more than 1,200 acres of farmland had been recovered through the clearing of irrigation channels and rehabilitation of canals at major irrigation sites. The commissioner added that the state government, in collaboration with the African Development Bank-supported Agricultural Transformation Agenda Support Programme (ATASP), had recovered more than 200 additional acres for irrigation. He said the government had secured approval to develop 11 mini dams and irrigation facilities across 11 local government areas. “When completed, these projects will provide about 2,000 additional acres of irrigable farmland in the state,” he said. Mahmoud further disclosed that the ministry had completed more than 70 milk collection centres to improve milk handling and storage in pastoral communities. He said the centres were equipped with storage facilities and solar-powered cooling systems to preserve milk before transportation to markets. The post Farmers-herders clashes reduced in Kano — Commissioner appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Don’t cause crisis in Obi’s camp, OK Movement warns NDC, Obidients
item.description: … As Camp faces setback amid rift By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AS Campaigns have begun ahead of 2027 general elections, the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has warned the Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council and the Obidient Movement not to cause friction in the camp of the NDC Presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Recall that crisis had last month reared its head between the leadership of the party and the support group when the OK Movement unveiled its presidential campaign council and the leadership of the party immediately took a swipe at the development as it rejected the composition of the Campaign Council. The NDC maintained that the role of support groups should be limited to supporting the party and its candidates, rather than assuming the functions of a political party. The OK Movement on its part, resisted the NDC’s position, saying it had a mandate to ensure that Obi and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso were elected in 2027. This led to strained relations between the two groups. Reacting to the development, the United Kingdom Coordinator of the OK Movement, Adebayo Brown, on Tuesday accused leaders of the NDC PCC and the Obidient Movement of encouraging divisions among groups associated with Peter Obi’s 2027 presidential ambition. Brown who urged the leaders to stop what he described as unnecessary political disputes, pleaded with them to focus on mobilising Nigerians, strengthening grassroots structures and preparing for the 2027 general elections, Adebayo Brown has accused the Coordinator of the Obidient Movement, Moses Paul, and the Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim, of allegedly allowing political disagreements to distract them from their organisational responsibilities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Brown said the two individuals should concentrate on rebuilding political structures, strengthening grassroots mobilisation and campaigning for the party’s candidates rather than engaging in what he described as unnecessary personal and political disputes. Brown who expressed concern over what he described as the continued targeting of the National Director-General of the OK Movement, Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu, by individuals expected to provide leadership within their respective organisations, however questioned the relevance of repeated claims by the Obidient Movement Coordinator that former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, and former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, had dissociated themselves from the OK Movement The statement is titled, ” Joblessnesss , Oblessness and lack of Leadership Capacity. “ Brown ‘s statement read, Two appointments have been given to individuals who now appear more interested in political disputes than in the responsibilities of their offices: one as Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and another as Director General of the NDC. “Ordinarily, one would expect people entrusted with such responsibilities to demonstra
item.dc:creator: Akinbayo Wahab
item.content:encoded: … As Camp faces setback amid rift By Henry Umoru ABUJA- AS Campaigns have begun ahead of 2027 general elections, the Obi-Kwankwaso (OK) Movement has warned the Nigeria Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council and the Obidient Movement not to cause friction in the camp of the NDC Presidential candidate, Peter Obi. Recall that crisis had last month reared its head between the leadership of the party and the support group when the OK Movement unveiled its presidential campaign council and the leadership of the party immediately took a swipe at the development as it rejected the composition of the Campaign Council. The NDC maintained that the role of support groups should be limited to supporting the party and its candidates, rather than assuming the functions of a political party. The OK Movement on its part, resisted the NDC’s position, saying it had a mandate to ensure that Obi and Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso were elected in 2027. This led to strained relations between the two groups. Reacting to the development, the United Kingdom Coordinator of the OK Movement, Adebayo Brown, on Tuesday accused leaders of the NDC PCC and the Obidient Movement of encouraging divisions among groups associated with Peter Obi’s 2027 presidential ambition. Brown who urged the leaders to stop what he described as unnecessary political disputes, pleaded with them to focus on mobilising Nigerians, strengthening grassroots structures and preparing for the 2027 general elections, Adebayo Brown has accused the Coordinator of the Obidient Movement, Moses Paul, and the Director-General of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) campaign, Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim, of allegedly allowing political disagreements to distract them from their organisational responsibilities ahead of the 2027 general elections. Brown said the two individuals should concentrate on rebuilding political structures, strengthening grassroots mobilisation and campaigning for the party’s candidates rather than engaging in what he described as unnecessary personal and political disputes. Brown who expressed concern over what he described as the continued targeting of the National Director-General of the OK Movement, Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu, by individuals expected to provide leadership within their respective organisations, however questioned the relevance of repeated claims by the Obidient Movement Coordinator that former Anambra State Governor, Peter Obi, and former Kano State Governor, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, had dissociated themselves from the OK Movement The statement is titled, ” Joblessnesss , Oblessness and lack of Leadership Capacity. “ Brown ‘s statement read, Two appointments have been given to individuals who now appear more interested in political disputes than in the responsibilities of their offices: one as Coordinator of the Obidient Movement and another as Director General of the NDC. “Ordinarily, one would expect people entrusted with such responsibilities to demonstrate a sense of urgency, focusing their energy on organising, mobilising, and campaigning for the party’s candidates. With the 2027 general elections approaching, the task ahead demands strategic thinking, effective coordination, and grassroots mobilisation. “Unfortunately, rather than concentrating on these critical responsibilities, their attention appears to be directed towards the National Director General of the OK Movement, Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu. “With only 76 days to the general elections, one would expect serious minded leaders to be preoccupied with building structures, strengthening grassroots engagement, and preparing for the enormous responsibility of electoral mobilisation. Instead, MO continues to make claims that HE Peter Obi and HE Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso have dissociated themselves from the OK Movement. “The question is simple: how does this constant repetition of such claims contribute to the success of the party or the democratic aspirations of Nigerians? ” The strength of the OK Movement is rooted in its ideology, principles, and core values—not in the approval of individuals or the political positions they occupy. “MO should concentrate on the mandate entrusted to him: rebuilding, revitalising, and restructuring the Obidient Movement. This is an opportunity to demonstrate leadership, capacity, and organisational competence. The task deserves his full attention, not a diversion into unnecessary personal and political disagreements. “We recognise and respect the tenacity, capacity, and integrity of Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu, National Director-General of the OK Movement, who has made significant sacrifices to build the movement into what it is today. “The journey has not been easy. He has invested considerable personal resources, time, energy, and commitment in the collective vision of the OK Movement. In the face of challenges, he has continued to stand for justice, equity, fairness, and the principles upon which the movement was established. “It is important to make one thing absolutely clear: Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu is a successful businessman and a committed advocate of workers’ interests. His commitment to the movement should not be misrepresented as a pursuit of personal gain. “Those who appear uncomfortable with his independence must understand that the OK Movement is an organisation built around principles and a collective vision, not the personal ambitions of any individual. “Furthermore, the Coordinator of the Obidient Movement does not automatically speak for HE Peter Obi, nor can he unilaterally determine or represent the interests of HE Peter Obi and HE Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso. Such positions should be established through clear and verifiable communication, not personal assertions.” Warning that the divisive rhetoric must stop, Adebayo Brown said, ” For the avoidance of doubt, the OK Movement and the Obidient Movement are not enemies. Neither is the OK Movement in conflict with the NDC. We have a common democratic challenge ahead, and the priority should be mobilising Nigerians, strengthening political structures, and working towards credible elections in 2027. “MO should therefore focus on the enormous responsibility before him. Rebuilding the Obidient Movement, strengthening its grassroots structures, and mobilising supporters require serious work, strategic planning, and measurable results. That is where his energy should be directed. “Nigeria is bigger than any individual, and the struggle for democracy is greater than personal disagreements. “We have advised Hon. John Ozyl Ughulu to disregard these distractions and remain focused on the work of building the OK Movement, strengthening its structures, and contributing meaningfully to the defence of Nigeria’s democracy. “The OK Movement will not be distracted, intimidated, or defined by the opinions of individuals. Our commitment remains justice, equity, fairness, credible elections, and a better Nigeria. The time for division is over. The time to work is now.” ENDS The post Don’t cause crisis in Obi’s camp, OK Movement warns NDC, Obidients appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Defence Minister welcomes reinstated permanent secretary
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Minister of Defence, General Christopher Gwabin Musa (Rtd), on Tuesday welcomed the Permanent Secretary of the Ministry, Mr Richard Pheelangwah, back to office following the lifting of his suspension and his reinstatement by the Federal Government. Musa expressed confidence in maintaining a cordial working relationship with the permanent secretary, stressing the need to build on their existing synergy to advance the ministry’s mandate. Pheelangwah, in his remarks, expressed appreciation for the opportunity to resume duty and pledged to discharge his responsibilities with renewed dedication, professionalism and commitment to national service. A statement by the minister’s Special Adviser on Media, Leah Katung-Babatunde, said the meeting reaffirmed the ministry’s commitment to institutional continuity, effective service delivery and the pursuit of Nigeria’s defence and security objectives. The post Defence Minister welcomes reinstated permanent secretary appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Insecurity: Borno Police nab 103 suspected criminals
item.description: By Ndahi Marama, Maiduguri The Borno State Police Command has arrested 103 suspected criminals in connection to combat substance abuse, violence, thuggery and other social vices. The arrests were carried out in Maiduguri metropolis between the months of October 29 to November 2nd, 2026, with support from its Rapid Response Squad (RRS) – Social Vices Unit. This was disclosed by the Police Public Relations Officer, ASP Keneth Daso in a statement he signed on Tuesday. item.title: How Trump could interfere in US midterm elections
item.description: State officials who run US elections are braced for possible intervention by President Donald Trump’s administration in Tuesday’s midterms – fearing federal authorities could disrupt voting, challenge ballot counts or try to block unfavorable results. Trump, whose Republicans face an uphill battle to keep control of Congress, has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and urged his party to “nationalize” voting in at least 15 places. The White House says it is protecting election security, and many of the feared scenarios remain hypothetical. The US Constitution gives the president no direct role in running elections, and courts have so far rebuffed the administration’s main legal challenges. Here are the key potential flashpoints: Who gets to vote The Justice Department has sued 30 states and the District of Columbia to obtain their voter registration lists, saying it needs them to find non-citizens. It has lost more than two dozen of those cases. It has also demanded that ballots be set aside from about 20,000 people in California and more than 400 in Washington state whom it suspects are non-citizens. The US Supreme Court rejected the California request, handing the Trump administration a snub a day before election day. Washington state has also refused the demand. Studies have repeatedly found non-citizen voting to be exceptionally rare. The Justice Department has warned election officials in every state that they could face prosecution if they knowingly allow non-citizens to vote. And Trump has offered $1 million for information leading to a voter fraud conviction, without giving details. At polling stations The Justice Department plans to send around 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states — its largest deployment ever. Monitoring is a decades-old practice, but Democrats and voting rights groups fear monitors could intimidate voters. The department says they will be unarmed, barred from interfering with voting and drawn from neither the FBI nor Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The administration says it is not planning operations targeting polling places, although Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has said ICE agents could serve warrants there. Trump has declined to rule out declaring a national emergency or invoking the Insurrection Act, which allows the president to deploy troops at home. A Civil War-era law bars troops and armed federal agents from polling places, and legal experts say an emergency declaration would not give the president power over elections. Counting the votes Federal agents could seek warrants or subpoenas for ballots, voting machines or records — potentially disrupting the count. In January, the FBI seized ballots and other 2020 election records in Fulton County, Georgia, a focus of Trump’s false claims that he won that year. item.content:encoded: State officials who run US elections are braced for possible intervention by President Donald Trump’s administration in Tuesday’s midterms – fearing federal authorities could disrupt voting, challenge ballot counts or try to block unfavorable results. Trump, whose Republicans face an uphill battle to keep control of Congress, has repeatedly questioned the integrity of US elections and urged his party to “nationalize” voting in at least 15 places. The White House says it is protecting election security, and many of the feared scenarios remain hypothetical. The US Constitution gives the president no direct role in running elections, and courts have so far rebuffed the administration’s main legal challenges. Here are the key potential flashpoints: Who gets to vote The Justice Department has sued 30 states and the District of Columbia to obtain their voter registration lists, saying it needs them to find non-citizens. It has lost more than two dozen of those cases. It has also demanded that ballots be set aside from about 20,000 people in California and more than 400 in Washington state whom it suspects are non-citizens. The US Supreme Court rejected the California request, handing the Trump administration a snub a day before election day. Washington state has also refused the demand. Studies have repeatedly found non-citizen voting to be exceptionally rare. The Justice Department has warned election officials in every state that they could face prosecution if they knowingly allow non-citizens to vote. And Trump has offered $1 million for information leading to a voter fraud conviction, without giving details. At polling stations The Justice Department plans to send around 1,000 election monitors to all 50 states — its largest deployment ever. Monitoring is a decades-old practice, but Democrats and voting rights groups fear monitors could intimidate voters. The department says they will be unarmed, barred from interfering with voting and drawn from neither the FBI nor Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The administration says it is not planning operations targeting polling places, although Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin has said ICE agents could serve warrants there. Trump has declined to rule out declaring a national emergency or invoking the Insurrection Act, which allows the president to deploy troops at home. A Civil War-era law bars troops and armed federal agents from polling places, and legal experts say an emergency declaration would not give the president power over elections. Counting the votes Federal agents could seek warrants or subpoenas for ballots, voting machines or records — potentially disrupting the count. In January, the FBI seized ballots and other 2020 election records in Fulton County, Georgia, a focus of Trump’s false claims that he won that year. Election officials warn that similar action during an active count could undermine safeguards tracking how ballots are handled. Trump could allege fraud involving mail-in ballots, voting machines or votes counted after election night, fueling demands for recounts or attempts to halt counting. But the US Supreme Court ruled in June that states may count mail ballots postmarked by election day that arrive afterward, and courts can intervene against unlawful disruption. After election day The Justice Department has sued Alaska to delay certification of its Senate race if Republican incumbent Dan Sullivan narrowly loses to Democrat Mary Peltola, citing a second candidate named Dan Sullivan who it says is trying to confuse voters, which he denies. Trump said he ordered the lawsuit. Experts say federal law does not allow the department to block certification, which courts can compel officials to carry out. Trump could pressure state officials to dispute results, as he did after losing the 2020 election. Experts warn unresolved disputes could also delay the seating of newly elected lawmakers in January. But courts have repeatedly upheld states’ authority over elections, and Democrats and voting rights groups have assembled legal teams to fight any interference. item.title: This space company is betting its future on a propellant available everywhere
item.description: Robert, Ryan, and Kirby Carlisle are three engineers who worked at SpaceX during the Falcon 9 era, seeing the revolution in the global launch industry from the inside. The brothers launched rockets, refurbished rockets, and sold rockets. But when it came time for them to leave SpaceX and start their own space company—a lifetime dream for the Carlisle brothers—they chose not to build rockets. Rather, they focused on spacecraft. In late 2022, the three Carlisles founded Argo Space to build infrastructure in space. Their vision was not just in-space transportation but also removing the need to use propellants from Earth to move around the heavens. They chose water, which is potentially harvestable on the Moon and found all over the Solar System, as a means of propulsion. Read full article Comments

item.title: Atiku accuses DSS of plotting to disrupt ADC rally in Sokoto
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the leadership of the Department of State Services, DSS, of recruiting protesters to create disorder in Sokoto and provide a pretext for imposing a curfew to stop the party’s campaign rally. Atiku said the alleged plot was part of a broader attempt by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration to frustrate opposition parties, undermine political competition and deny Nigerians the freedom to choose their leaders ahead of the 2027 general election. Briefing journalists in Abuja on Tuesday, the former vice president alleged that public facilities meant for campaign activities had been blocked and logistical support withheld in Sokoto, describing the developments as deliberate efforts to deny the ADC a level playing field. He said information available to the party indicated that protesters were being mobilised from an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road, with trucks deployed to strategic locations, including a roundabout. According to him, the protesters were causing gridlock, threatening commuters and beating some residents, while some had moved away from the roundabout to find shade. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform,” Atiku said. “Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis.” He called on security officers allegedly involved in the mobilisation to stop immediately and return to their constitutional duty of impartial service. Atiku accused the Tinubu administration of devoting much of its energy over the past three and a half years to weakening credible opposition, alleging that its strategy of absorbing former opposition figures into the APC was aimed at reducing Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name. The former vice president also linked the alleged obstruction of the rally to the economic hardship facing Nigerians, saying the government should be defending its record on the rising cost of food, transport, fuel, electricity and other essentials rather than trying to stop opposition campaigns. “Families are struggling to feed their children, pay school fees and keep their businesses alive,” he said. “That is the record this government should be defending before the people, instead of trying to stop a rally.” Atiku pledged that an ADC government would make life affordable through policies to support local production, strengthen food production, create jobs and reduce the cost of doing business. item.content:encoded: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President and presidential candidate of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Atiku Abubakar, has accused the leadership of the Department of State Services, DSS, of recruiting protesters to create disorder in Sokoto and provide a pretext for imposing a curfew to stop the party’s campaign rally. Atiku said the alleged plot was part of a broader attempt by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration to frustrate opposition parties, undermine political competition and deny Nigerians the freedom to choose their leaders ahead of the 2027 general election. Briefing journalists in Abuja on Tuesday, the former vice president alleged that public facilities meant for campaign activities had been blocked and logistical support withheld in Sokoto, describing the developments as deliberate efforts to deny the ADC a level playing field. He said information available to the party indicated that protesters were being mobilised from an office behind Zenith Bank on Koko Road, with trucks deployed to strategic locations, including a roundabout. According to him, the protesters were causing gridlock, threatening commuters and beating some residents, while some had moved away from the roundabout to find shade. “This is not intelligence work. It is political interference dressed in official uniform,” Atiku said. “Security agencies exist to protect Nigerians and uphold the law, not to recruit protesters or help a political party manufacture a crisis.” He called on security officers allegedly involved in the mobilisation to stop immediately and return to their constitutional duty of impartial service. Atiku accused the Tinubu administration of devoting much of its energy over the past three and a half years to weakening credible opposition, alleging that its strategy of absorbing former opposition figures into the APC was aimed at reducing Nigeria to a one-party state in all but name. The former vice president also linked the alleged obstruction of the rally to the economic hardship facing Nigerians, saying the government should be defending its record on the rising cost of food, transport, fuel, electricity and other essentials rather than trying to stop opposition campaigns. “Families are struggling to feed their children, pay school fees and keep their businesses alive,” he said. “That is the record this government should be defending before the people, instead of trying to stop a rally.” Atiku pledged that an ADC government would make life affordable through policies to support local production, strengthen food production, create jobs and reduce the cost of doing business. He said the party would also pursue a targeted production subsidy tied to fuel refined in Nigeria, aimed at providing measurable relief to consumers while strengthening domestic industry. The ADC presidential candidate accused the APC of resorting to intimidation and obstruction after what he described as the failure of its last rally in Kaduna, saying the party should have taken the outcome as a warning that Nigerians were withdrawing their confidence. These are the last kicks of a dying horse,” Atiku said. “The more this government tries to silence the people, the clearer it becomes that it has already lost their confidence.” Atiku said the 2027 general election would be a defining moment in Nigeria’s democratic history, insisting that the contest was not merely between political parties or candidates but between a government he accused of indifference to citizens’ suffering and Nigerians determined to make their votes count. He vowed that the ADC would resist what he described as administrative roadblocks and underhand manoeuvres designed to exclude the opposition, adding that he would be in Sokoto on Wednesday to address residents. “I will be in Sokoto tomorrow, God willing, to address the good people of the state,” he said. He urged residents to remain peaceful and avoid being provoked into violence, while calling on security agencies to protect commuters, residents and rally participants without favour. Atiku also warned that officers who colluded in suppressing political freedom would be held accountable under the law, while pledging support for those who refused to be used against democracy. He urged Nigerians to remain resolute in defending their democratic rights, declaring that the country belonged to its people and not any political party or temporary occupant of power. item.title: EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun
item.description: The Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC) says it has uncovered an illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals in the Ogere area of Ogun State. The Commission disclosed that the operation, carried out on Saturday, October 31, 2026, by operatives of its Lagos Zonal Directorate 2, followed intelligence gathering and surveillance on the activities of illegal sludge oil refiners. The development was contained in a statement issued on Tuesday by the EFCC Head of Media and Publicity, Dele Oyewale. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC According to the Commission, the refinery was deserted when operatives stormed the premises, following an earlier crackdown on four illegal lithium processing plants in the area. However, they discovered waste products from the refining process, as well as underground tanks believed to have been used for heating and processing sludge oil. “Two of the underground tanks inspected contained substances suspected to be Automotive Gas Oil (AGO), otherwise known as diesel,” the statement said. The EFCC said preliminary investigations showed that the operators sourced sludge oil, also known as black sludge, from Warri in Delta State and Port Harcourt in Rivers State before transporting it to the facility in Ogere for processing. The illegal oil refinery allegedly operated by Chinese nationals. X/@officialEFCC It explained that further investigations indicated that the operators subjected the sludge oil to intense heat, allowing lighter petroleum components to pass through a series of chambers and filters in a process believed to produce Automotive Gas Oil (AGO) for sale in the Nigerian market. The Commission added that security personnel at the facility told its operatives that the Chinese operators never disclosed their identities or the name of the company behind the operation. Operatives of the Lagos Zonal Directorate 2 have since taken over the premises as investigations continue to establish the identities of the operators, ownership of the facility and the full extent of the suspected illegal activities and economic sabotage. The post EFCC Uncovers Chinese-Operated Illegal Oil Refinery In Ogun appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Astronaut and Earth
item.description: CSA CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Joshua Kutryk is pictured during the Oct. 29, 2026, spacewalk. The International Space Station was soaring 267 miles above the South Atlantic Ocean at the time of this photograph. Kutryk and NASA astronaut Anil Menon installed a new roll-out solar array on the space station and performed some get-ahead work for their next spacewalk , which will take place on Nov. 5, 2026. The pair will install the eighth and final roll-out solar array; together, the eight arrays will increase the station’s available power by up to 30%. Image credit: CSA

item.title: Password manager mSecure tells users to change passwords, won't say why
item.description: Password manager mSecure has warned customers to change their passwords, reset two-factor authentication, and potentially remove their passkeys after detecting suspicious activity, but it has not explained what happened or whether anyone's secrets were exposed. In an email sent to customers on November 3, seen by The Register , US-based developer mSeven Software said it launched an investigation after discovering something amiss with its password management application. "mSeven Software ('mSeven') recently learned of suspicious activity associated with the mSecure password management application," the company wrote. "In response, mSeven quickly launched an investigation, took steps to mitigate the issue, and engaged external cybersecurity experts to assist." The company has yet to answer what the suspicious activity involved, when it occurred, or whether attackers accessed customer information. Its advice to customers, however, suggests that they should take this seriously. "Given the potential security implications, mSeven recommends that you immediately take steps to protect all confidential information stored within the mSecure password management application," the email continued. "This may include changing passwords, resetting or re-enrolling two-factor authentication methods, or removing existing passkeys." For anyone with hundreds of passwords stored in mSecure, that's potentially hours of work. And without knowing what happened, customers have no way of telling which credentials they actually need to replace. The warning has understandably gone down poorly with customers, who have taken to mSecure's support forum demanding answers. "Please provide more context to your email below advising there has been a security breach," one customer wrote. "It is not acceptable to offer the vague advice 'take steps'. Please state what remedial action is required, and what data was compromised." Others are wondering whether they're expected to spend the next several days changing every password they've ever saved. "I have over 800 passwords in mSecure, is the email saying I need to change all of them!" another customer asked. A separate user, who said they had more than 500 passwords stored in the application, questioned whether the warning applied to every two-factor authentication method and passkey associated with their accounts, or just those used to access mSecure itself. The confusion has also spilled onto Reddit , where customers have shared copies of the vague notification and questioned what might have happened. mSeven has yet to respond to The Register 's questions, leaving customers to guess whether their data has actually been compromised or the company is simply being cautious. That's not exactly reassuring from a business whose entire purpose is keeping other people's secrets safe. The company's email concludes: "We regret any inconvenience that this may cause." For customers contemplating hundreds of password resets, "inconvenience" may b

item.title: UEFI bootkit infected fully patched Windows machines. Is Microsoft to blame?
item.description: In 2023, malware tracked as BlackLotus became the first publicly documented in-the-wild UEFI bootkit capable of bypassing Secure Boot on fully updated Windows 11 systems. With the industry-wide chain-of-trust mechanism subverted, the malware was able to run malicious code before Windows was fully loaded and many security defenses were operational. Microsoft had already patched the vulnerability that BlackLotus exploited in 2022. In 2023 and 2024, Microsoft issued additional updates. The first added a new certificate that no longer trusted the vulnerable boot managers. The second provided the means to revoke trust in the digital certificate used to sign older vulnerable Windows boot managers. The organizations infected by the new bootkit, which is tracked under the name BlackX, had installed all of these patches. So how did they fall victim? UEFI bootkit refresher Before discussing the incident further, a brief review of BlackLotus and UEFI malware is in order. Short for Unified Extensible Firmware Interface , UEFI is firmware that runs immediately after a computer is turned on. One of its main jobs is to load system configuration settings, identify and initialize hardware components, and prepare the computer to start its OS. Read full article Comments

item.title: GhostBSD 26.2 takes the fright out of FreeBSD with a friendlier installer
item.description: GhostBSD, the easiest-to-install flavor of FreeBSD for the daemon-curious desktop dabbler, is back with a fresh update. GhostBSD 26.2-R15.1p6 , to give it its slightly unwieldy full version number, is based on FreeBSD 15.1. It brings a new installer, full-disk encryption support, a smaller installation image, and fixes across its desktop tools. FreeBSD 15.1 was released back in June , and at the time of writing, it's the most recent point release of FreeBSD. The original plan was that FreeBSD 15.1 would include the option of installing KDE Plasma directly from the setup program, so that the OS would have a graphical desktop from its very first boot. However, this feature isn't ready just yet. That gap inspired Daemonarchy, which we covered late last month . But its Omarchy-derived, keyboard-driven tiling desktop can feel unfamiliar even to experienced Linux users accustomed to conventional desktops. GhostBSD has different goals. It brings Linux-like desktop convenience to FreeBSD: a live graphical environment to explore before installation, a graphical installer, and tools for managing software and updates. These conveniences are familiar to desktop Linux users, but a standard FreeBSD installation takes more work. Its text-mode installer leaves users to install and configure a graphical desktop themselves, if they want one. This is just how the BSD family does things, and most BSD users we've talked to regard it as standard operating procedure and see nothing wrong with it. For Linux users who are curious about how things are on the other side of the FOSS Unix fence, though, those extra steps can form formidable barriers. GhostBSD is an attempt to lay down a welcome mat. The standard edition of GhostBSD installs the MATE desktop, and the downloads page also offers a community-maintained version with Xfce instead. As the project said it would back in February, this release uses the XLibre fork of the X.org X11 server. That's one fewer desktop than when we last tried GhostBSD in August 2025 . That release also offered the Mac OS X-like Gershwin environment. There are practical hardware fixes too. The release notes list improvements for Intel AX200 Wi-Fi cards, open networks, password alerts, and non-ASCII network names, while USB HID support is enabled by default. Where has Gershwin gone? Gershwin remains in active development , so we asked project lead Joe Maloney why it wasn't included. "It has been difficult to find time to package for GhostBSD. It's the only distro I have ever packaged for," Maloney said. He added that rapid contributions from AppImage creator Simon Peter, known as probono, had made packaging increasingly difficult. He also pointed to the fact that GhostBSD project lead Eric Turgeon is developing his own environment too: the Mocka desktop . Mocka is still in its very early stages – alpha version 0.0.2 appeared early last month – but the plan is that when it's ready, it will become GhostBSD's default desktop. For now, the only a
item.dc:creator: Liam Proven
item.content:encoded: GhostBSD, the easiest-to-install flavor of FreeBSD for the daemon-curious desktop dabbler, is back with a fresh update. GhostBSD 26.2-R15.1p6 , to give it its slightly unwieldy full version number, is based on FreeBSD 15.1. It brings a new installer, full-disk encryption support, a smaller installation image, and fixes across its desktop tools. FreeBSD 15.1 was released back in June , and at the time of writing, it's the most recent point release of FreeBSD. The original plan was that FreeBSD 15.1 would include the option of installing KDE Plasma directly from the setup program, so that the OS would have a graphical desktop from its very first boot. However, this feature isn't ready just yet. That gap inspired Daemonarchy, which we covered late last month . But its Omarchy-derived, keyboard-driven tiling desktop can feel unfamiliar even to experienced Linux users accustomed to conventional desktops. GhostBSD has different goals. It brings Linux-like desktop convenience to FreeBSD: a live graphical environment to explore before installation, a graphical installer, and tools for managing software and updates. These conveniences are familiar to desktop Linux users, but a standard FreeBSD installation takes more work. Its text-mode installer leaves users to install and configure a graphical desktop themselves, if they want one. This is just how the BSD family does things, and most BSD users we've talked to regard it as standard operating procedure and see nothing wrong with it. For Linux users who are curious about how things are on the other side of the FOSS Unix fence, though, those extra steps can form formidable barriers. GhostBSD is an attempt to lay down a welcome mat. The standard edition of GhostBSD installs the MATE desktop, and the downloads page also offers a community-maintained version with Xfce instead. As the project said it would back in February, this release uses the XLibre fork of the X.org X11 server. That's one fewer desktop than when we last tried GhostBSD in August 2025 . That release also offered the Mac OS X-like Gershwin environment. There are practical hardware fixes too. The release notes list improvements for Intel AX200 Wi-Fi cards, open networks, password alerts, and non-ASCII network names, while USB HID support is enabled by default. Where has Gershwin gone? Gershwin remains in active development , so we asked project lead Joe Maloney why it wasn't included. "It has been difficult to find time to package for GhostBSD. It's the only distro I have ever packaged for," Maloney said. He added that rapid contributions from AppImage creator Simon Peter, known as probono, had made packaging increasingly difficult. He also pointed to the fact that GhostBSD project lead Eric Turgeon is developing his own environment too: the Mocka desktop . Mocka is still in its very early stages – alpha version 0.0.2 appeared early last month – but the plan is that when it's ready, it will become GhostBSD's default desktop. For now, the only available module is a dock for the MATE desktop, but the curious can follow its development on the GitHub project page . There may be no Gershwin included, but GhostBSD 26.2 offers MATE 1.28, and there's also a community-supported version with Xfce 4.20 instead. We tried the default MATE edition, and it works as well as ever. It defaults to a dark theme and the classic two-panel GNOME 2 desktop layout. The System menu in the top panel has an Administration submenu with a few of the project's own apps that aren't from upstream FreeBSD: "BE Station" for managing system boot environments, "Software Station" for browsing and installing applications, and "Update Station" for updates. We regularly hear from users growing tired of the Linux vendors' headlong rush into Rust, Wayland, systemd, containerized app formats, and so on. Some are curious about whether FreeBSD offers a usable alternative. GhostBSD is the easiest way to get a complete, ready-to-use graphical FreeBSD desktop. There is a price to pay for switching to FreeBSD: for a start, most proprietary Linux apps, from Chrome to Slack, are not available here. Hardware compatibility needs more checking than on mainstream Linux, especially with recent GPUs and Wi-Fi adapters. If Windows gaming is a priority, this isn't the obvious choice. But if you can live without those proprietary apps and find suitable open source replacements, FreeBSD is a viable alternative – and GhostBSD takes much of the setup work out of trying it. ®

item.title: Pan-African School Games 2026: Celebrating Young Talent, School Pride and New Opportunities
item.description: The Pan-African School Games 2026 brought together young athletes from schools across Lagos for three days of swimming, athletics and football, celebrating sporting talent, school pride and the opportunities that organized competition can create for children and young people. Held at James Hope College, Lekki, from 16 to 18 October, the second edition of the Games featured the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. Students competed for individual honours and school points while gaining valuable experience in a structured, multi-sport environment. The competition also welcomed sporting stakeholders and scouts, reinforcing the wider ambition of the Pan-African School Games: to give young athletes a platform where their abilities can be demonstrated, recognized and developed. Building on the Inaugural Games The second edition of the Pan-African School Games built on the foundation established by the inaugural Games in 2025, continuing the vision of creating meaningful sporting opportunities for young athletes. The 2026 edition welcomed schools and student-athletes for three days of swimming, athletics and football, providing a platform for competition, talent development and school pride. Beyond the sporting results, the Games continued to advance a broader ambition: to connect schools, athletes, sporting stakeholders and educational institutions while creating opportunities for young people to develop their abilities and explore future pathways through sport. Day One: Swimming Opens the Games Swimming opened the competition, bringing young swimmers together for races across the U-11, U-13 and U-15 categories. The opening day set the pace for the Games as athletes took to the pool to test their abilities, pursue strong performances and earn points for their schools. The races highlighted the preparation, discipline and technique required to compete, while providing young swimmers with valuable experience in a formal sporting environment. For many of the students, the opportunity to compete alongside athletes from other schools added to the significance of the experience. Each race contributed to the overall competition, with schools beginning their campaigns for medals and category honours. Day Two: Athletics Puts Young Athletes to the Test Athletics took centre stage on the second day, with track and field events testing the speed, strength, coordination and technique of the young competitors. Athletes competed in running, jumping and throwing events, earning points for their schools as the standings developed. Each discipline presented a different challenge, giving students opportunities to demonstrate their abilities and compete for individual and team honours. The athletics programme added another dimension to the Games, highlighting the variety of talent within the participating schools and the value of giving young athletes opportunities to develop through competition.
